Required work:
1. Introduce explicit audit/instrumentation/internal-role session-entry semantics or equivalent boundary metadata.
2. Stop Garden/admin prompt edits from injecting normal-channel system notes via appendSystemNote().
3. Exclude audit/instrumentation entries from context assembly and extraction by default.
4. Audit callers that persist tool observations or system notes into shared session history.
5. Add regression coverage across persistence, context build, and extraction paths.

Acceptance:
- Operator/system instrumentation can be reviewed without becoming conversational context.
- Extraction no longer sees operator/audit artifacts unless explicitly intended.
- Prompt edits and similar admin actions stop leaking into ordinary companion turns.
- Tests prove the new non-conversational boundary is fail-closed.

description:

title: Preserve authored system/tool semantics through context-to-provider conversion
description:
Summary:
Session storage preserves system/tool roles, but the LLM context conversion path collapses them before provider dispatch. entriesToMessages() emits ContextMessage.role = system for system notes and tool observations, yet contextMessagesToPiMessages() rewrites every system context message to a pi-ai user message. This makes system and tool-authored context appear as partner-authored text to the model, violating the charter's message ontology and authorship integrity rules.

Confirmed code surfaces:
- src/session/manager/context-support.ts
- src/llm/message-conversion.ts
- src/types.ts
- src/memory/extraction/chunk-compose.ts
- src/memory/extraction/runtime-helpers.ts

Required work:
1. Preserve authored transport semantics through the context-to-pi-ai/provider boundary instead of collapsing system context entries into user.
2. Decide and encode how tool observations should be represented on the provider side without impersonating the user.
3. Update extraction transcript/token-trigger helpers to use authored/internal provenance rather than treating every non-assistant entry as user speech.
4. Add regression tests proving system/tool/internal entries are not presented to the model or extractor as partner-authored utterances.

Acceptance:
- Context/system entries remain distinguishable at provider dispatch time.
- Extraction transcript formatting and token-trigger accounting no longer label system/tool entries as user speech.
- Tests cover session-to-context-to-provider and session-to-extraction paths.
notes:
Additional confirmed surfaces from follow-up investigation:
- Session storage is not the main collapse point; later conversion paths rewrite systemNote/system to user in src/agent/messages.ts:125 and src/llm/message-conversion.ts:10.
- Tests currently lock in the collapse in src/llm/message-conversion.test.ts:28.
- There is no general originalType reconstruction path in src/session/turn-provenance.ts:67 and src/agent/messages.ts:185.
close_reason: Implemented on refactor-pt2 with authored system/tool role preservation through provider conversion and extraction formatting. System/internal notes no longer collapse into partner-authored user speech; extraction transcript formatting and trigger accounting now preserve authored lanes. title: Make memory retrieval relevance-terminated and add a pre-LLM extraction signal gate
description:
Summary:
Memory retrieval currently ranks candidates, then fills selection until the token budget ceiling is reached. There is no relevance floor that stops marginal memories from being added when budget remains. Extraction triggering is driven by message interval and/or context token threshold; there is no cheap pre-LLM gate that skips low-signal turns before calling the extraction model.

Confirmed code surfaces:
- src/memory/retrieval.ts
- src/memory/extraction/runtime-helpers.ts
- src/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts
- src/memory/extraction/signals.ts

Required work:
1. Add a relevance floor or equivalent post-ranking stop condition so retrieval can stop before budget is full when remaining candidates are too weak.
2. Keep budget as a ceiling, not the primary reason to include marginal memories.
3. Add a cheap pre-LLM extraction gate that can skip turns lacking emotional shift, relational change, explicit preference/boundary/episodic signal, novelty, or minimum content length.
4. Add tests for sparse-relevance retrieval and low-signal extraction skip behavior.

Acceptance:
- Retrieval can return fewer memories than budget allows when the remaining ranked candidates are below threshold.
- Extraction can skip calling the LLM entirely for low-signal turns.
- Telemetry shows whether retrieval stopped on relevance floor vs budget and whether extraction was skipped by the pre-LLM gate.
notes:
Additional confirmed surfaces from follow-up investigation:
- Retrieval currently fills by token budget in src/memory/retrieval.ts:911 and src/memory/retrieval.ts:1807, with tests locking that behavior in src/memory/retrieval.test.ts:971.
- Extraction triggers only on interval/context-threshold in src/memory/extraction/runtime-helpers.ts:48 and src/memory/extraction.ts:171.
- System notes currently contribute to extraction trigger token counting via src/memory/extraction/runtime-helpers.ts:25-29.

title: Decide PostgreSQL embedding storage/search strategy behind MemoryStorePort
description:
Summary:
The new PostgreSQL memory adapter currently persists embeddings as DOUBLE PRECISION[] and performs similarity scoring in process. Before more backend-specific tuning lands, we need an explicit architectural decision on whether PostgreSQL embeddings remain array-backed for now or move to pgvector with database-side indexing/search. The decision must preserve the MemoryStorePort seam and avoid leaking raw database details into callers.

Decision inputs:
- current implementation in src/faculties/memory/postgres-store.ts and src/persistence/postgres/migrations.ts
- operational expectations for PostgreSQL extension availability
- parity requirements with SQLite sqlite-vec / FTS5 behavior
- contributor goals for scalable fast retrieval in PostgreSQL

Decision record should answer:
1. Is pgvector required, optional, or deferred for the supported PostgreSQL path?
2. If optional, how is selection configured without hidden fallback?
3. What fail-closed behavior applies when configured pgvector support is unavailable?
4. What parity and migration expectations exist versus the current DOUBLE PRECISION[] shape?

Validation:
- Record the decision in repo docs/charter-adjacent architecture docs if behavior/support policy changes.
- npm run lint if any code/docs with lint coverage are touched.
close_reason: Decision accepted for the supported PostgreSQL path: PostgreSQL memory embeddings/search should use pgvector behind MemoryStorePort rather than keeping an array-backed production mode. Missing required pgvector support is a fail-closed configuration/runtime error, not an implicit fallback to app-side DOUBLE PRECISION[] scanning. Implementation remains tracked in PSFN-80xh.4.

title: Implement pgvector-backed PostgreSQL memory embeddings behind MemoryStorePort
description:

acceptance_criteria:
- `ChannelAdapterPort` exists as a first-class production seam with a stable registry and factory boundary.
- Compatibility shims are removed or fully contained behind adapters.
- Channel consumers depend on the port or registry seam rather than concrete adapter maps.
- New channels can be plugged in without editing unrelated runtime call sites.
close_reason: Completed: extracted ChannelAdapterPort/ChannelAdapterRegistryPort and rewired startup, gateway, API, and prompt routing consumers

Primary files include `src/core/session/continuity.ts`, `src/core/session/manager.ts`, `src/core/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts`, `src/system/trust/policy.ts`, and operator/session inspection surfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
- `CrossChannelContinuityPort` exists as a first-class production seam.
- Continuity producers and consumers depend on the port instead of `UserContinuityStore` and ad hoc helper calls.
- Storage and policy details are moved behind adapters or collaborating domain services.
- Alternate continuity storage and backends can be introduced without rewriting session and turn logic.
close_reason: Completed: extracted CrossChannelContinuityPort over storage, merge policy, mirroring, and provenance parsing; rewired session manager/context/Garden consumers; validated focused continuity suites

title: Extract pluggable EmbeddingProviderPort across transformers, Ollama, and external runtimes

This work must make embeddings pluggable across current transformer-backed, Ollama-backed, and external/gateway-backed implementations without rewiring memory/extraction code, and remove any assumptions that the default backend is the only operational path. Primary files include `src/core/agent/contracts.ts`, `src/faculties/memory/embedding.ts`, `src/boundary/gateway/client.ts`, `src/faculties/memory/retrieval.ts`, `src/faculties/memory/extraction.ts`, and memory writer/migration code.

- Memory/retrieval/extraction code depends on the port instead of a concrete/default embedding runtime.
- At least two implementations are validated through injection-friendly tests or wiring, covering current local and remote/provider-backed paths.
- Backend-specific assumptions such as transformer-only behavior do not leak into the core interface.
notes: Secondary backend-readiness dependency: embeddings must be injectable so memory storage and retrieval are not implicitly coupled to a single local embedding runtime while storage moves toward PostgreSQL.
close_reason: Completed: promoted EmbeddingProviderPort across memory/runtime consumers and validated local plus gateway-backed implementations

title: Finish missing charter port extraction for pluggable runtime backends
description:
Summary:
The charter requires first-class pluggable port families so core concerns can be swapped without cross-repo surgery. Current code only exposes exact charter seams for `SessionJournalPort`, `CredentialVaultPort`, `SandboxExecutionPort`, and `ShardExecutionPort`. The rest are missing, renamed, or collapsed into concrete classes such as `LLMProvider`, `EmbeddingService`, `SystemConfigRepository`, `PromptLayerStore`, `PromptRegistryStore`, `MemoryStore`, `CoreMemoryStore`, `ConfirmationQueue`, `NtfyNotifier`, `ChannelAdapter`, `UserContinuityStore`, `GatewayClient`, and `BoundedSubagentLaunchPort`.

Why now:
This refactor is supposed to make the system ready for pluggable contributor/storage backends including PostgreSQL, multiple embedding providers, and external integrators. Thin alias ports are not enough. Each bead under this epic must produce a real seam that callers depend on directly, move the current default implementation behind an adapter, and make alternative implementations possible without rewriting call sites.

Primary files currently involved:
- docs/PSFN_PROJECT_CHARTER.md
- src/core/agent/contracts.ts
- src/system/config/system-config-repository.ts
- src/core/identity/prompt-store.ts
- src/core/identity/prompt-registry.ts
- src/faculties/memory/store.ts
- src/faculties/core-memory/store.ts
- src/boundary/gateway/client.ts
- src/system/capabilities/confirmation-queue.ts
- src/core/tools/ntfy.ts
- src/channels/backplane/types.ts
- src/core/session/continuity.ts
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/bounded-subagent-contract.ts
- src/faculties/shards/artifact-policy.ts
- satellites/openhome/host/adapter.ts
- satellites/wyoming/host/runtime.ts

Existing exact charter ports already present and not the primary gap in this epic:
- `SessionJournalPort`
- `CredentialVaultPort`
- `SandboxExecutionPort`
- `ShardExecutionPort`
acceptance_criteria:
- Every missing charter port in this epic exists as a first-class seam in production code.
- Core/runtime call sites depend on the port, not a concrete class or a thin compatibility shim.
- The current implementation is moved behind an adapter/factory rather than remaining the implicit only path.
- The resulting ports are sufficient to plug alternate backends/providers/adapters into storage, memory, prompting, channels, and agentic execution without cross-repo surgery.
close_reason: all steps complete

title: Testing hardening program: browser E2E, runtime boot coverage, and anti-pattern removal
description:
Summary: Execute a structured testing-hardening program to make PSFN test results correspond to real product behavior. The current suite has useful backend/unit coverage but still allows broken operator flows to ship because Garden has no browser E2E, split runtime has no real end-to-end boot test, several so-called wiring tests are source-text grep assertions instead of behavior tests, and multiple critical entrypoints/god files lack direct behavioral coverage. This epic owns the remediation work required to restore trust in test results.

Primary objectives:
1. Add real browser-driven Garden E2E coverage for basic operator flows.
2. Add real split-runtime and full-runtime boot/readiness coverage.
3. Replace source-grep wiring tests with behavioral/reachability tests.
4. Add stronger coverage around critical oversized entrypoint and orchestration files.
5. Ensure test names and categories accurately describe what they prove.

Files and surfaces in scope:
- admin-ui/**
- src/index.ts
- src/runtime.ts
- src/gateway-main.ts
- src/agent-main.ts
- src/channels/admin/**
- src/channels/api/**
- src/bootstrap/**
- src/agent/substrate-agent/**
- vitest.config.ts
- package.json
- scripts/**
- docs/ and audit docs only where test docs/commands need correction

Implementation lanes:
1. Browser E2E foundation
   - Introduce a real browser test harness (Playwright or equivalent) for Garden.
   - Cover login, logout, redirect-to-login, dashboard load, settings load, settings save, and basic chat-cockpit flow.
   - Verify cookie/session/auth behavior from a browser, not mocked requests.
2. Runtime boot and split-mode coverage
   - Add a real launcher/startup smoke that boots gateway + agent and proves ready-state plus one basic operator flow.
   - Add direct entrypoint startup/teardown tests for src/index.ts, src/gateway-main.ts, and src/agent-main.ts where practical.
   - Prove admin/bootstrap/chat readiness through real process boundaries.
3. Anti-pattern removal
   - Audit and replace source-grep tests of the form readFileSync(...).toContain(...) and similar text-presence assertions that pretend to validate wiring.
   - Replace them with runtime reachability, constructor invocation, or observable-behavior tests.
   - Rename or reclassify any remaining tests so they do not overclaim.
4. High-risk file coverage
   - Add direct behavioral coverage for critical large files and entrypoints that currently have weak or no direct tests, especially agent-main.ts, gateway-main.ts, runtime.ts, bootstrap/parity.ts, admin/api-routes.ts, and Garden settings page behavior.
   - Prioritize the flows most likely to break manual operator review.
5. Test taxonomy and trust restoration
   - Distinguish unit, request-level integration, smoke, in-process integration, and true E2E clearly in scripts/docs.
   - Stop calling in-process harnesses full E2E unless they actually cross the real system boundaries.
   - Make failures actionable and fail closed instead of allowing optional-pass states that hide broken UX.

Acceptance criteria:
- The repo has at least one real browser E2E suite for core Garden/operator flows.
- The repo has a real split-runtime or equivalent boot/readiness test that exercises actual runtime boundaries.
- Source-grep wiring assertions are removed or dramatically reduced and no longer treated as proof of runtime behavior.
- Critical entrypoint/admin surfaces have direct behavioral coverage instead of string-presence checks.
- Script names/docs accurately reflect whether a test is unit, smoke, integration, or true E2E.
- Manual operator review should no longer be the first place basic admin/runtime wiring failures are discovered.

Example before -> after:
- Before: a test reads src/agent-main.ts and checks that "new ModuleLoader(" exists in the file.
- After: a test boots the relevant startup path and proves ModuleLoader is constructed and used via observable behavior or controlled spy injection.

Source context:
- Primary audit report: PSFN_TESTING_AUDIT.md
- Discovered from: PSFN-2oth (combined testing audit report)

title: Bug: continuity watchdog health probe fails under authenticated API mode
description: Summary: The continuity watchdog added in PSFN-vtyj probes GET /health without any API credential, but ApiServer authenticates /health unless ALLOW_INSECURE_LOCAL_API=true. In authenticated deployments the watchdog will treat 401 responses as health failures and can trigger false restart loops. Files to modify: scripts/ops/continuity-watchdog-healthcheck.mjs, src/channels/api/server.ts, docs/operations/runtime-mode-runbook.md, docker/docker-compose*.yml as needed. Implementation steps: 1. Add authenticated health probing support (for example API key header or dedicated loopback-only health credential). 2. Preserve fail-closed behavior when auth is required. 3. Document the supported auth model for the watchdog and verify both secure and insecure-local modes. Example: when API_KEY is set and ALLOW_INSECURE_LOCAL_API is false, the watchdog should still receive 200 from /health instead of 401-driven restart escalation. Discovered while double-checking PSFN-vtyj closure.
close_reason: Completed: merged authenticated watchdog health probe fix (continuity-watchdog uses API key in secure mode, supports insecure-local mode). Validation on phase-v: npx vitest run src/channels/api/server.test.ts --silent (59 pass), node scripts/ops/continuity-watchdog-smoke.mjs (pass), docker compose config checks (pass in worker validation).

title: Fix gateway git repoRoot misbinding to workspace path
description:
Summary: In split/gateway mode, repo_status/repo_diff/repo_apply_patch are routed through GatewayGitOps to gateway-hosted GitOps, but gateway-main.ts instantiates GitOps with repoRoot=workspaceRoot instead of the code repository root. If WORKSPACE_PATH points outside the git worktree, git commands execute in a non-repo directory and fail with fatal: not a git repository. Even when workspace is nested under the repo, repo_apply_patch resolves file writes relative to workspace rather than repo root.

Files to modify:
- src/gateway-main.ts
- optional shared startup/bootstrap helper if repo root should be centralized
- tests under src/git/** or src/gateway/** covering split mode repoRoot/workspaceRoot divergence

Implementation steps:
1. Separate git repo root from workspace root in gateway startup; keep fs policy workspace-scoped.
2. Instantiate gateway GitOps with the actual repository root (or an explicitly validated GIT_REPO_ROOT setting), not WORKSPACE_PATH.
3. Add regression tests proving gateway git tools succeed when workspace is outside the repo but configured repo root points at a real worktree.
4. Add a fail-closed startup error if configured git root is not a git worktree.

Example:
Before: WORKSPACE_PATH=/tmp/ws causes repo_status -> fatal: not a git repository.
After: fs.read/fs.write remain rooted at /tmp/ws while git commands run against the configured repository root.
close_reason: Completed: gateway split mode now resolves and validates git repo root via GIT_REPO_ROOT/auto-detect, binds GitOps to repo root (not workspace root), and fails closed on invalid/non-top-level git roots. Regression tests: src/git/repo-root.test.ts, src/git/gateway-rpc-path.test.ts (workspace/git root divergence case), plus targeted vitest and eslint passes.

description:

4. Add telemetry for queued, parallel, skipped, and cancelled tool executions so streaming/tool latency can be audited.

After: compatible tool calls run concurrently, while stateful or mutating tools still serialize on their exclusivity key.

title: Fix shard spawning regression limiting parallel sub-agents to one active shard
description:
Summary: Parent-turn shard spawning is no longer truly parallel even though ShardManager itself supports multiple active shards. When the model emits multiple `spawn_shard` tool calls in one assistant turn, they are executed serially, so only one shard runs at a time and the runtime no longer behaves like multi-shard fan-out.

Root cause discovered:
- `src/shards/manager.ts` still permits concurrent shard execution and existing unit tests only cover direct `ShardManager.spawn()` parallel calls.
- The actual parent tool loop is delegated to `@mariozechner/pi-agent-core`.
- In `node_modules/@mariozechner/pi-agent-core/dist/agent-loop.js`, `executeToolCalls()` iterates tool calls with `for (...) { await tool.execute(...) }`, which serializes sibling `spawn_shard` calls.
- Result: multiple shard tool calls in one parent turn do not overlap, despite `src/shards/tools.ts` claiming they do.

Files to modify:
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts or a local agent-loop wrapper/patch module
- src/shards/tools.ts (description/docs if behavior contract changes)
- shard/agent integration tests under src/agent/** or src/shards/**

Implementation steps:
1. Add a local workaround/override for the parent tool-execution loop so sibling `spawn_shard` calls can execute as one parallel batch while preserving existing fail-closed behavior for other tools.
2. Keep non-shard tools sequential unless there is explicit proof wider parallel execution is safe.
3. Add a regression test at the parent-agent/tool-loop level proving 2-3 `spawn_shard` calls from a single assistant message overlap in time.
4. Verify runtime wiring still registers `spawn_shard` from a real entrypoint path (`src/bootstrap/composition.ts`).

Example:
Before: assistant emits shard A, shard B, shard C tool calls; A runs to completion, then B, then C.
After: assistant emits shard A/B/C; all three shard executions start before the first one finishes, subject to configured shard limits.
close_reason: Completed via PSFN-yt8f.1/.2: parent-loop shard fan-out now overlaps for sibling spawn_shard calls while non-shard tools remain sequential, with regression coverage for overlap/fail-closed and bootstrap wiring reachability.

title: Block unauthorized promotion to primary trust level
description:
Summary:
Prevent unauthorized escalation to `primary` trust in contact mutation paths.

Why:
If any external or misconfigured path can set `primary`, a non-owner identity can inherit highest-trust behaviors. This is a high-impact authorization flaw.

Files to modify:
- src/contacts/store.ts
- src/contacts/tools.ts
- src/channels/admin/services/identity-service.ts
- src/channels/api/server.ts
- src/contacts/store.test.ts
- src/channels/api/server.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Add a single guard in trust mutation primitives that denies `primary` assignment unless target identity matches configured owner mapping.
2. Enforce the same guard in both `setTrustLevel` and `upsertContact` paths (no bypass route).
3. Reject caller-provided `primary` in API/admin payloads unless an explicit privileged operator control path is used.
4. Emit audit events for denied/allowed primary-trust changes.
5. Add tests covering direct mutation, upsert path, API payload spoofing, and valid owner path.

Example:
Before: untrusted contact can be upserted with `trustLevel=primary`.
After: mutation is rejected with explicit authorization error unless identity is mapped to owner.
close_reason: Completed: enforced central primary-trust mutation guard across upsert/setTrustLevel, blocked caller-provided primary trust spoofing in API payloads, emitted allow/deny mutation audit signals, and added regression coverage for unauthorized/authorized paths.

title: Sanitize compaction summaries before system prompt injection
description:
Summary:
Treat compaction summaries as untrusted data and prevent prompt-injection persistence into system prompt assembly.

Why:
Compaction summaries can carry attacker-controlled instructions that persist across turns when injected into system prompt context, steering future behavior and tool usage.

Files to modify:
- src/session/manager.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/identity/prompt-composer.ts
- src/session/manager.test.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Mark compaction-summary content as untrusted at generation and retrieval boundaries.
2. Wrap inserted summary blocks in explicit non-executable tags (for example `<untrusted_context>`), with fixed guard text forbidding instruction execution from that block.
3. Strip/neutralize control markers that can escape wrapper boundaries.
4. Harden compaction prompt and insertion path so summaries remain factual data, not policy/instruction carriers.
5. Add regression tests with malicious summary payloads proving no system instruction override occurs.

Example:
Before: summary text is concatenated directly into system prompt body.
After: summary is embedded as inert untrusted context data and cannot alter instruction hierarchy.
close_reason: Completed: compaction summaries are now marked/wrapped as untrusted context with guard enforcement and boundary neutralization; malicious-payload regressions added for session manager and substrate prompt handoff.

title: Harden shutdown durability path and scheduler stop semantics
description:
Summary: Shutdown paths can become non-retriable after first failure; signal handlers fire async shutdown without robust error handling; scheduler can overlap ticks and stop without draining; session store mutates in-memory state before durable append.

Files to modify: src/runtime.ts, src/agent-main.ts, src/gateway-main.ts, src/scheduler/scheduler.ts, src/session/store.ts, src/session/store/journal-runtime.ts, src/session/continuity.ts.

Implementation steps:
1. Make shutdown steps fail-soft and retryable with step-level timeouts and finally fences.
2. Add reentrancy guards + `.catch` in signal handler shutdown invocations.
3. Ensure scheduler stop drains/joins active tick work before returning.
4. Apply write-ahead semantics for session append or rollback in-memory mutation on durable write failure.

Example:
Before: append fails after memory mutation, restart loses accepted turns.
After: durable append succeeds before in-memory commit, or mutation is rolled back.
close_reason: Completed: hardened shutdown retry semantics, signal-safe stop flow, scheduler drain behavior, and session append durability protections with tests. Validation: runtime/scheduler/session test suites passed in integration.

title: Make extraction scheduling resilient to unhandled rejections and crash-recovery loss
description:
Summary: Extraction/refresh promise chains can emit unhandled rejections; crash-recovery extraction failures can be swallowed and then permanently skipped after graceful marker update.

Files to modify: src/memory/extraction.ts, src/memory/extraction/runtime-helpers.ts, src/memory/extraction/orchestrator.ts, src/runtime.ts, src/session/store/crash-recovery.ts.

Implementation steps:
1. Wrap fire-and-forget extraction jobs with explicit rejection handling and observability.
2. Make crash-recovery extraction idempotent with durable retry bookkeeping on failure.
3. Prevent graceful-marker advancement from suppressing unresolved recovery backlog.
4. Add restart scenario tests covering first-failure then graceful shutdown sequence.

Example:
Before: first retroactive extraction fails once, future restarts skip it forever.
After: failed recovery remains pending until successful completion or explicit operator dismissal.
close_reason: Completed: hardened extraction fire-and-forget rejection handling, crash-recovery backlog retry tracking, and graceful-marker suppression for unresolved backlog; added restart regression coverage. Validation: runtime/store/extraction test suites passed in integration.

title: Harden split-mode wiring (voice, modules, memory, shutdown)
description:
Summary: Gateway+substrate split wiring still has correctness drift in module registry pathing, Wyoming provider gating, API voice websocket enablement checks, memory extraction dependencies, and shutdown lifecycle markers.

Files to modify: src/gateway-main.ts, src/agent-main.ts, src/bootstrap/composition.ts, src/modules/loader.ts, src/modules/registry.ts, shared runtime helper modules consumed by split startup.

Implementation steps:
1. Normalize module registry path resolution for the split startup path so registry reads/writes are deterministic.
2. Reuse one provider-enabled gating primitive for Wyoming STT/TTS in gateway+agent startup (no ad-hoc local checks).
3. Gate API voice websocket exposure on fully wired runtime availability in split mode.
4. Ensure split-mode memory extraction is always wired with required session/contact stores.
5. Make split-mode shutdown sequence durable and complete (graceful marker + module loader shutdown + retry-safe teardown).

Example:
Before: split mode can advertise capabilities that are only partially wired, with mode-specific drift.
After: split mode only advertises/live-enables capabilities when fully wired, with deterministic startup and shutdown behavior.
close_reason: Completed: split-mode wiring hardening for module registry pathing, runtime/provider gating, API voice websocket readiness gating, and durable split shutdown sequencing with targeted wiring tests. Validation: bootstrap/registry/runtime helper tests passed in integration.

title: Fix voice websocket race/retry semantics and backpressure
description:
Summary: Voice websocket frame handling is concurrent without sequencing; stage timeout/retry does not cancel underlying work; session start can race into duplicate STT streams; transcript queue is unbounded.

Files to modify: src/voice/transports/websocket/server.ts, src/voice/transports/websocket/runtime.ts, src/voice/policy/reliability.ts, src/voice/connectors/stt/deepgram-stream.ts.

Implementation steps:
1. Add per-connection/frame serialization or bounded work queue with backpressure.
2. Implement cooperative cancellation (AbortSignal) for timed-out stage attempts before retries.
3. Make `session.start` idempotent with in-progress sentinel and atomic state transitions.
4. Bound transcript queue and apply drop/backpressure policy with metrics.

Example:
Before: timeout triggers retry while original LLM/TTS still running.
After: timed-out attempt aborts first; retry starts only after confirmed cancellation.
close_reason: Completed: added websocket frame serialization/backpressure, cooperative timeout cancellation, idempotent session.start, and bounded transcript queues with targeted regression coverage (voice websocket/reliability/deepgram tests passed).

title: Make agent turn processing globally serialized per runtime context
description:
Summary: Per-channel locking does not prevent cross-channel overlap that mutates shared Substrate agent state (`setSystemPrompt`, `setTools`, message replacement), risking context poisoning and telemetry misattribution.

Files to modify: src/agent/substrate-agent.ts, src/lifecycle/turn-contention.ts, src/agent/event-bridge.ts, channel adapters using contention manager.

Implementation steps:
1. Introduce runtime-level turn mutex (or per-agent key lock) across all channel adapters.
2. Remove mutable global event-bridge channel context in favor of per-request scoped context objects.
3. Add stress test with concurrent API + Discord turns asserting no context/tool-stream crossover.

Example:
Before: channel A and B can overlap until downstream busy check, after shared state is already mutated.
After: second turn waits/rejects before any shared agent mutation occurs.
close_reason: Stale under current gateway-mode architecture: substrate is single-runtime/single-channel in prod path, so cross-channel event-bridge overlap vector is currently out of scope.

title: Harden API auth boundaries (no unauthenticated mode, restrict CORS, bind caller identity)
description:
Summary: API currently permits unauthenticated operation when key is unset, allows permissive `*` CORS, and trusts caller-provided session/user identifiers. This enables local drive-by abuse and cross-client identity collision.

Files to modify: src/channels/api/server.ts, src/channels/api/voice-websocket-runtime.ts, src/channels/http/auth.ts, relevant config docs/env validation.

Implementation steps:
1. Require explicit secure dev flag for keyless mode; otherwise fail fast at startup if API auth secret missing.
2. Replace wildcard CORS with allowlist config and deny credentialed cross-origin by default.
3. Derive principal/session identity from authenticated token/session, not caller-controlled headers/query fields.
4. Add tests for rejected unauthenticated access and identity spoof attempts.

Example:
Before: no `API_KEY` => requests pass auth branch.
After: startup error unless `ALLOW_INSECURE_LOCAL_API=true` and loopback-only bind enforced.
notes: Gateway-only topology reduces direct browser attack surface, but keep fail-closed auth/CORS/identity hardening for mis-exposure scenarios.
close_reason: Completed: fail-closed API auth defaults with explicit insecure local mode guardrails, CORS allowlist policy, and principal-bound caller identity; added auth/CORS/spoofing tests plus env/docs updates. Validation: vitest pass in integration run (API/auth test subset).

title: Fix ntfy unicode title header ByteString crash
description:
Summary: notify.ntfy could throw in gateway mode when title contains non-ASCII characters (e.g. emoji) because undici enforces ByteString header values. This surfaced as "Cannot convert argument to a ByteString ... value ... greater than 255".

Files:
- src/gateway/ntfy-notifier.ts

3. Add regression test that sends unicode title and asserts request succeeds without crash.
close_reason: Implemented UTF-8-to-ByteString header encoding for ntfy title in gateway + tool notifier, sanitized CR/LF, and added unicode-title regression test. ntfy and gateway tests pass.

title: Add evidence-support and contradiction-aware terms to memory retrieval scoring
description:
Summary: Extend retrieval scoring to downweight weakly supported or contradicted memories so emotionally salient but fragile memories do not dominate prompts.

Files to modify:

- src/memory/* tests and scoring telemetry

2. Integrate term into final ranking formula alongside similarity/recency/emotional-weight/importance.
3. Add safeguards for single-source low-confidence memories unless explicitly queried.
4. Expose per-term score breakdown in retrieval trace logs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contradicted/superseded memories are consistently downranked by default.
- High-emotion low-support memories no longer dominate unrelated retrievals.
- Retrieval trace includes support/contradiction term contributions.
close_reason: Completed

title: Implement L0/L2 tombstone + redaction event pipeline with deterministic replay semantics
description:
Summary: Make expunge/redaction coherent by appending tombstone/redaction events (no destructive rewrite), then applying them consistently in retrieval and replay across L0 and derived stores.

Files to modify:
- src/session/* (L0 redaction event append/read paths)
- src/memory/* (deleted_at/superseded_by + tombstone linkage)
- src/replay/* or equivalent reconstruction path

Implementation steps:
1. Define redaction/tombstone event schema targeting TurnID and/or derived artifact IDs.
2. Add append-only redaction events in L0 journal.
3. Apply tombstones by default in retrieval and reconstruction/replay.
4. Ensure derived stores can be deterministically rebuilt with tombstones applied.

Acceptance criteria:
- Redacted turns/memories are excluded by default from retrieval/context.
- Replay/rebuild honors tombstones deterministically.
- No physical L0 rewrite is required for normal redaction operations.
close_reason: Completed: added append-only session journal turn tombstone events (redact/restore), default filtering of tombstoned turns in session + turn-record reads, channel-index/tail-read safeguards, search-index realignment, and regression coverage for redact/restore determinism.

title: Add central EligibilityGate for runtime tier and capability enforcement
description:
Summary: Consolidate tier/capability enforcement so any model-purpose call, worker, scheduler task, or tool action must pass one central EligibilityGate check.

Files to modify:
- src/capabilities/*
- src/agent/*
- src/llm/* (purpose routing/fallback path checks)
- src/scheduler/* and background worker entrypoints

Implementation steps:
1. Introduce RuntimeTier + EligibilityGate API with allow/deny reason codes.
2. Integrate gate checks into model purpose resolution, async worker launch, scheduler execution, and tool invocation boundaries.
3. Fail closed on unknown/unsupported combinations.
4. Emit denial/allow telemetry for observability and audits.

Acceptance criteria:
- Tier N cannot execute Tier N+1 behaviors through any code path.
- Denials are explicit and logged with actionable reason codes.
- No bypass paths remain in background/scheduler execution.
close_reason: Implemented central EligibilityGate and wired LLM/scheduler/post-turn/tool boundaries with fail-closed purpose checks, explicit denial reason codes, and regression tests; build+full test suite passing.

title: Implement immutable TurnSnapshot contract between fast loop and slow/background loops
description:
Summary: Prevent ghost drift by freezing a TurnSnapshot at turn start and requiring all in-turn reads to use snapshot state only. Post-turn/background workers may write only new versions for future turns.

Files to modify:
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/session/manager/*
- src/memory/* (retrieval version pointer usage)
- src/contacts/*, src/concerns/* (snapshot readers)

Implementation steps:
1. Define TurnSnapshot (contact/trust snapshot, active concerns snapshot, emotional snapshot, memory index version pointer, prompt stack version pointer).
2. Capture snapshot at turn start and thread through context composition/retrieval/prompting.
3. Block in-turn reads from mutable live stores once snapshot is established.
4. Ensure slow-loop writes produce next-version state only.

Acceptance criteria:
- Same input + same snapshot yields deterministic retrieval/context decisions.
- Background updates during a turn do not change in-flight turn behavior.
- Post-turn writes are visible only to subsequent turns.
close_reason: Integrated immutable TurnSnapshot capture across prompt/session/memory reads with persisted version pointers; validated via targeted snapshot regressions and build.

title: Define canonical TurnRecord schema + TurnID and wire turn provenance references
description:
Summary: Introduce a first-class TurnRecord object keyed by globally unique TurnID (prefer UUIDv7/time-ordered) and require downstream artifacts to reference TurnID instead of ad hoc session-range references.

Files to modify:

- src/session/* (L0 recording + linkage)

- src/memory/*, src/contacts/*, src/scheduler/* (reference fields)

Implementation steps:
1. Define TurnRecord with user/assistant messages, tool calls, context manifest pointer, internal-state snapshot pointer, extracted memory IDs, concern/contact deltas, and version pointers.
2. Generate TurnID at turn start and propagate through telemetry + persistence.
3. Update memory extraction outputs and related artifacts to store TurnID provenance.
4. Add migration/backfill strategy for existing records lacking TurnID.

Acceptance criteria:
- New turns persist canonical TurnRecord entries.
- Downstream artifacts reference TurnID.
- Provenance queries resolve from memory/contact/scheduler records back to original turn.
close_reason: Completed

title: Phase V foundations: canonical turn provenance, loop contracts, policy gates, and evidence-aware memory
description:
Summary:
Establish Phase V foundations for deterministic, replayable, and policy-safe cognition by introducing canonical turn provenance, explicit fast/slow loop contracts, centralized runtime tier enforcement, coherent redaction/tombstone semantics, and evidence-aware retrieval scoring.

Why:
Current architecture has strong building blocks (L0 sessions, L2 memory, contact/trust, scheduler, prompt composition), but provenance and mutation boundaries are not yet first-class. As Phase V adds context planners, metacog, and additional asynchronous cognition, missing structural contracts will create race conditions, nondeterminism, and unverifiable provenance.

Scope:
- Canonical TurnRecord + globally unique TurnID as join key across subsystems.
- Immutable TurnSnapshot at turn start for deterministic fast-loop execution.
- Central EligibilityGate so runtime tiers/capability levels are enforced uniformly.
- Redaction/tombstone model across L0 and derived stores without destructive rewrite.
- Retrieval scoring support term for contradiction/supersession/evidence strength.

Out of scope:
- Full Phase V product features (metacog UX, advanced planners, etc.) beyond foundational contracts and enforcement.

Acceptance criteria:
1) All turn-adjacent artifacts can be traced via TurnID and replayed deterministically.
2) Mid-turn background mutations cannot alter in-flight turn reads.
3) Tier-raising behaviors are denied centrally when runtime tier disallows them.
4) Redaction/tombstones are applied consistently in retrieval and replay.
5) Retrieval scoring uses evidence support/contradiction metadata to suppress weakly supported memories.
close_reason: Completed: all Phase V foundation child tasks are closed including 04dt.4 tombstone/redaction replay semantics; provenance, immutable snapshots, eligibility gating, retrieval evidence scoring, and deterministic turn redaction are now landed.

title: Normalize OpenRouter model IDs in LiteLLM mode for wildcard routing
description:
Summary: In LiteLLM mode, provider=openrouter with vendor-qualified model IDs (e.g., google/gemini-3-flash-preview) was sent without openrouter/ namespace. LiteLLM wildcard routing in this environment is configured under openrouter/*, so requests returned no healthy deployments.

Files:
- src/agent/stream-adapter.ts
- src/agent/stream-adapter.test.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.test.ts (expectation updates for normalized IDs)

Steps:
1. Normalize OpenRouter model IDs in LiteLLM mode to openrouter/<model> when model ID is vendor-qualified.
2. Preserve non vendor-qualified aliases unchanged.
3. Add regression tests for normalization and adjust affected expectations.
close_reason: Implemented model ID normalization for OpenRouter in LiteLLM mode (vendor-qualified IDs become openrouter/<model>), added stream-adapter tests for normalization behavior, and updated affected SubstrateAgent test expectations. All targeted tests pass.

title: Per-purpose model primary/fallback slot configuration + admin UX controls
description:
Summary: Replace the current slot-mapping model configuration with a canonical data-driven model registry and top-level Model Management UX. All model settings and routing controls must live in one dedicated model page, with no legacy slot indirection and no backward-compat shims.

Required model purposes:
- chat
- background
- extraction
- summary
- reasoning
- import_processing
- longContext
- vision
- moa

Core product requirements:
1. Model sources: allow adding any number of models from OpenRouter, direct provider APIs, and local runtimes (for example Ollama/llama.cpp), using pi-agent-core provider metadata where available.
2. Purpose tagging: each model can be tagged for multiple purposes.
3. Primary and secondary per purpose: exactly one primary model per purpose; remaining tagged models are secondary candidates.
4. Ranked fallback heuristic: for each purpose, fallback order combines (a) primary flag, (b) operator drag/drop preference order, (c) capability fit (context window etc.), and (d) cost weighting.
5. Cost tracking and budgets: track per-model token usage/cost by service/process; enforce daily/monthly budget policy and surface hold/notify behavior when budget blocks expensive routes.
6. UX model page: move all model controls into one top-level Model Management page with data-driven controls (DDL, sliders, chips, drag/drop ordering). Each model row has top summary (provider/serving source, context/response limits, thinking flags) with expandable advanced settings (temperature, top_p/top_k, repetition/frequency penalties, etc.).

Architecture constraints:
- JSON for settings/config, .env for secrets only.
- No legacy compatibility layer, no hidden migration shims, fail closed on missing/invalid config.
- No hardcoded model variables in UI logic; schema/data-driven rendering and binding.

Files to modify (expected):
- src/types.ts and model/settings schema modules
- src/settings/* model persistence/validation
- src/llm/* routing/fallback/selection policy
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts and model-purpose call sites
- src/channels/admin/api-routes.ts and services
- admin-ui model/settings routes/components
- tests across settings, routing, gateway/admin API, and UI state

Implementation steps:
1. Define canonical model registry schema (providers, capabilities, purpose tags, primary flags, rank, cost metadata, budget policy links).
2. Remove legacy purpose->slot remap path and route directly from purpose tags + ranking heuristic.
3. Implement deterministic per-purpose selector with fail-closed validation and single-primary enforcement.
4. Implement token/cost accounting + daily/monthly budget gates + notify/hold signaling hooks.
5. Build top-level Model Management UI and migrate all model-related controls there.
6. Add regression coverage for persistence, selection order, budget-block behavior, and UI contract.

Acceptance:
- All model mapping and settings are configured from the dedicated model page.
- Per-purpose primary/secondary tagging is deterministic and test-covered.
- Budget policy can block costly model use and surfaces actionable notification state.
- No legacy slot mapping path remains reachable in production code.
close_reason: Completed: canonical modelRegistry + per-purpose selector/fallback + dedicated Models UX + budget metering/gating + no-legacy integration guardrails, with regression coverage across settings/routing/runtime/admin APIs/UI build checks.

title: Gateway vision fetch loses GatewayClient binding (rpcInstance undefined)
description:
Summary: In gateway mode, SubstrateAgent extracted llmProvider.webFetchBinary into a standalone function before invoking it. For GatewayClient this dropped method binding, so rpcInstance was undefined and Discord image fetch failed with a TypeError.

Files:
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.test.ts

Steps:
1. Call webFetchBinary via provider object method access to preserve instance binding.
2. Add regression test where webFetchBinary checks object context and fails if called unbound.
3. Validate gateway-mode vision tests pass.
close_reason: Fixed: webFetchBinary now called via bound provider method path in SubstrateAgent; added regression test proving method context binding is preserved; gateway vision tests pass.

title: Vision routing misses some Discord image attachments and recovery can still return empty
description:
Summary: Discord image turns can bypass vision routing when attachment contentType is missing or generic even though URL/name indicates image (e.g. CDN links with format params). Also, if the initial vision call fails and first recovery prompt returns empty, turn can still end silently.

Files: src/agent/substrate-agent.ts, src/agent/substrate-agent.test.ts, src/agent-main/gateway-message-handlers.ts, src/agent-main/gateway-message-handlers.test.ts

Steps: (1) Add image MIME inference in SubstrateAgent from attachment URL/name including query format and extension heuristics. (2) Use inferred image MIME for vision routing and image block resolution. (3) Add one extra strict recovery retry if first recovery is still empty, with diagnostics. (4) Add lightweight attachment-count telemetry in gateway message handler logs. (5) Add regression tests for inferred-image routing and second-recovery path.
close_reason: Implemented: inferred image MIME routing from attachment URL/name including format query parameters, gateway-only binary fetch behavior (no direct fallback when gateway fetch is present), strict second-pass non-empty recovery for failed vision turns, and gateway Discord attachment telemetry with regression tests.

title: Vision turns can fail silently when configured LiteLLM vision deployment is unavailable
description:
Summary: When a vision turn routes to a model with no healthy LiteLLM deployment, pi-agent-core surfaces an assistant message with empty content and stopReason=error. The runtime currently sends no user-visible reply, causing silent failure in Discord/Telegram image turns.

Files to modify:
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Detect empty assistant text on vision turns and capture stopReason/errorMessage from latest assistant message.
2. Emit explicit warning telemetry with model/stopReason/error details.
3. Run one recovery prompt using chat slot model (fallback) so user gets a response even when vision slot deployment is unavailable.
4. Recovery instruction should ask the model to clearly state image-processing failure and request resend (model-authored response, not hardcoded outbound message).
5. Add regression test for: first assistant reply empty error -> second recovery reply sent via chat model.

Example:
Before: vision turn -> empty response (no message sent).
After: vision turn fails -> recovery prompt -> assistant replies that image could not be processed and asks for resend.
close_reason: Implemented: detect empty vision assistant output with stopReason/errorMessage diagnostics; run one recovery prompt on chat model slot to produce explicit model-authored image-failure response; added regression test for empty vision reply recovery path.

title: Audit and remove hardcoded fallback assistant text injection
description:
Summary: Audit the codebase for any fallback paths that fabricate assistant/user-facing text (putting words in the assistant’s mouth) when upstream data is missing or a tool/input fails. Replace those paths with explicit telemetry + transparent status signaling that preserves model autonomy.

Files to modify:
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/agent/stream-adapter.ts
- src/channels/discord/adapter.ts
- src/channels/telegram/adapter.ts
- src/channels/admin/services/settings-service.ts
- src/channels/admin/api-routes.ts
- src/gateway/methods/*.ts (any response-fallback paths)
- Tests under src/agent/*.test.ts, src/channels/*/*.test.ts, src/gateway/methods/*.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Search for hardcoded fallback content injected into assistant-visible/user-visible paths (e.g., synthetic guidance strings, forced canned replies, synthetic user text beyond transport markers).
2. Classify each instance as allowed transport normalization vs disallowed speech fabrication.
3. Remove/replace disallowed instances with structured diagnostics (logs/events/metadata) and non-fabricating behavior.
4. Add regression tests proving failed attachment/tool/input paths do not inject assistant wording and instead surface transparent failure state.
5. Document accepted fallback policy in docs/architecture or docs/operations so future changes follow the same rule.

Example:
Before: on image load failure, code appends hardcoded instruction text into turn content telling assistant what to say.
After: no injected speech; runtime logs/metadata indicate image-not-loaded and assistant responds from its own reasoning/context.
close_reason: Completed: removed canned Discord fallback reply in gateway message handler; now logs + audit diagnostics only (discord.message.error) with regression tests.

title: Unify settings persistence: single source of truth per config domain
description:
Summary: Runtime/admin currently uses overlapping settings surfaces (settings.json + models.json + service-level save paths), which creates drift and restart-time overrides. We need a single source of truth per module and deterministic sync semantics.

Problem statement:
- Model settings can be written through multiple handlers/APIs.
- Some paths persist settings.json but not models.json (or vice versa), so restart load order can revert saved values.
- This violates Phase IV/Phase V maintainability goals and creates operator distrust.

Files to modify:
- src/settings.ts
- src/config/models-config.ts
- src/runtime.ts
- src/agent-main.ts
- src/channels/admin/handlers/settings.ts
- src/channels/admin/services/settings-service.ts
- src/channels/admin/api-routes.test.ts
- src/channels/admin/server.test.ts
- docs/architecture/settings-persistence.md (new)

Implementation steps:
1. Define authoritative ownership: one file per config domain (models, scheduler, trust, capabilities, general runtime).
2. Enforce one-way load order and remove cross-file overwrite behavior for owned domains.
3. Consolidate all admin save paths to shared persistence primitives that update exactly the owned domain file(s).
4. Add startup drift detection logs when conflicting values are detected (temporary guardrail until migration complete).
5. Add migration logic for legacy mixed-state files and tests covering restart persistence.
6. Document persistence contracts and allowed writers for each domain.

Example:
Before: save vision model in admin API, restart, stale models.json overrides it.
After: model domain has one authoritative file and all save paths route through one writer; restart never reverts saved values.

Acceptance criteria:
- No domain has overlapping authoritative files.
- Restart preserves values set by every admin save path.
- Tests cover save + restart + reload for model settings across all APIs.
- Conflict detection/telemetry exists during migration window.
close_reason: Completed: enforced domain-owned settings persistence, added drift detection/migration guards, unified admin save paths, and documented ownership contract; full gate passed.

title: Admin settings API did not sync models.json causing restart model reverts
description:
Summary: PATCH /api/admin/settings (settings service path used by modern admin/garden UX) persisted settings.json but did not sync models.json. On restart, runtime loads models.json after settings.json, so stale models.json overwrote recently saved model roster changes (including vision).

Files modified:
- src/channels/admin/services/settings-service.ts
- src/channels/admin/api-routes.test.ts

Implementation steps completed:
1. In settings service updateSettings(), after applying saved settings, sync models.json via saveModelsConfig using runtime model catalog + role assignments.
2. Add API regression test proving a PATCH payload containing modelCatalog/modelRoleAssignments persists vision mapping into models.json.

Example:
Before: set vision slot in admin, save, restart, vision reverted due stale models.json.
After: save updates both settings.json and models.json so restart preserves vision mapping.
close_reason: Synced models.json writes in admin settings API and added regression coverage

title: Admin settings save can reset vision model to chat fallback
description:
Summary: Saving settings from the admin roster form could silently reset modelRoster.vision to the chat slot model when vision assignment was missing or omitted. This caused operators to pick a vision model, hit save, and end up back on chat defaults (for example z-ai/glm-5).

Files modified:
- src/settings.ts
- src/channels/admin/templates/settings.ts
- src/settings.test.ts
- src/channels/admin/templates.test.ts

Implementation steps completed:
1. Ensure normalizeEditableSettings sets a stable vision assignment, preferring dedicated vision slot when present.
2. Ensure vision roster resolution prefers vision assignment or vision slot instead of unconditional chat fallback.
3. Add vision to admin template default role assignments and default to vision slot when catalog has one.
4. Add regression tests for normalize and template render behavior.

Example:
Before: select vision model in UI, save, then modelRoster.vision is rewritten to chat model.
After: save preserves dedicated vision slot/model and no silent reset.
close_reason: Fixed vision assignment/save fallback so admin save no longer resets to chat model

title: Vision turns silently degrade when configured vision model is text-only
description:
Summary: Discord and Telegram vision turns can route to purpose=vision but still send text-only payloads when the configured vision model lacks image input support. This currently fails silently and looks like random vision misses.

Files to modify:
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.test.ts
- optional: src/agent/stream-adapter.ts if capability helpers are reused

Implementation steps:
1. Detect when a turn is routed as vision but resolved model.input does not include image.
2. Emit warn-level telemetry and logging with model/provider and channel context so operators can see why image understanding failed.
3. Emit warn-level logging when image attachments were present but none were resolved into image blocks.
4. Add tests proving mismatch and drop scenarios emit diagnostics without regressing existing routing behavior.

Example:
Before: purpose=vision with model z-ai/glm-5 (input text-only) silently strips image blocks and replies quickly as if no image existed.
After: logs clearly state that vision routing used a text-only model and image inputs were dropped.
close_reason: Completed: vision-purpose models now forced image-capable in stream-adapter for LiteLLM paths; added warnings when purpose=vision resolves to text-only model input; added warning when image attachments exist but none resolve. Targeted tests pass (stream-adapter + substrate-agent).

title: Phase V: Split production Purrsephone runtime into dedicated folders and containers
description:
Summary: Separate production Purrsephone from continuous/dev runtime paths to prevent cross-contamination of data, config, and process state. Production should live in dedicated directories and container definitions with explicit boundaries.

Files to modify:
- docker-compose*.yml (or compose manifests)
- Dockerfile* (as needed for prod/dev split)
- scripts/start/restart tooling used by runtime self-restart
- .env.example and runtime mode docs
- docs/operations/ (new runbook for prod vs continuous stacks)
- persistence path configuration wiring (if currently shared)

Implementation steps:
1. Define canonical directory layout for production vs continuous/dev (dataDir, workspace, logs, backups, temp).
2. Split container services and volumes so production has isolated mounts, networks, and restart policy.
3. Introduce explicit runtime mode markers so self-restart logic uses correct entry command per mode.
4. Add safeguards against accidental shared mounts/secrets between environments.
5. Document boot, restart, backup, and rollback flows for production separately.

Example:
Before: production and continuous runtimes may share base paths/process assumptions.
After: production runs in isolated container + storage paths, continuous/dev runs separately with no shared mutable state.
close_reason: Completed via PSFN-b6nq.1/.2/.3: mode-aware runtime path contract, split compose/container topology, and operations runbook/script safeguards for prod vs continuous runtime.

title: Phase V: Add controlled beads issue-management tool access for agent runtime
description:
Summary: The runtime agent currently cannot create/update beads because shell.exec is policy-denied in gateway mode. Add a first-class, policy-scoped beads tool path so the agent can manage issues safely without unrestricted shell access.

Files to modify:
- src/gateway/policy.ts
- src/gateway/protocol.ts
- src/gateway/methods/ (new beads method module, e.g. beads.ts)
- src/tools/registry.ts (or equivalent tool registration layer)
- src/tools/session.ts (if tool exposure plumbing is centralized there)
- src/channels/admin/ (optional audit visibility for bead actions)
- tests under src/gateway/methods/ and tool integration tests

Implementation steps:
1. Define typed gateway methods for minimal beads operations: ready/show/create/update/close/sync (or an explicitly narrowed subset).
2. Implement strict argument validation and policy gates (allowlisted subcommands only, bounded args, no arbitrary shell passthrough).
3. Add audit telemetry for each bead action (actor, action, target issue id, result).
4. Expose these methods as agent tools with clear capability tokens (e.g., issue_read, issue_write, issue_close).
5. Add tests for allowed operations, denied operations, malformed payloads, and audit output.

Example:
Before: agent tries shell.exec -> DENY when attempting bd create.
After: agent calls typed beads.create tool -> allowed by policy and audited.
close_reason: Completed: added policy-scoped beads gateway methods/tools with allowlisted actions, validation, audit hooks, and tests; full gate passed.

title: Discord vision: accept Discord CDN host variants in attachment allowlist
description:
Summary: Vision attachment host allowlist in SubstrateAgent is too strict (exact-only for cdn.discordapp.com/media.discordapp.net). Discord may emit attachment URLs on other discordapp.net/discordapp.com CDN subdomains, causing image turns to silently downgrade to text/retrieval.

Files to modify:
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Expand allowlist logic from exact host set to safe suffix allowlist for Discord CDN domains.
2. Keep HTTPS requirement and existing byte/mime checks unchanged.
3. Add regression test proving gateway vision fetch path accepts a discordapp.net CDN variant host.

Example:
Before: https://images-ext-1.discordapp.net/... rejected by host check.
After: same URL accepted and routed through vision fetch path.
close_reason: Expanded Discord vision host gate to allow trusted discordapp.com/discordapp.net CDN variants (not just exact hosts) and added regression test for images-ext-1.discordapp.net vision routing.

title: Phase V: Add missing regression tests for model configuration controls
description:
Summary: Add comprehensive regression coverage for model configuration controls so runtime/provider behavior is stable across direct + gateway execution paths and admin settings updates.

Why: Current coverage is incomplete for key model knobs (thinking enable/disable, thinking effort, temperature, top_p, top_k, repetition penalty, and related sampling controls), which risks silent behavior drift after config/API changes.

Files to modify:
- src/llm/stream-adapter.test.ts
- src/llm/client.test.ts
- src/gateway/methods/llm.test.ts
- src/channels/admin/api-routes.test.ts
- src/channels/admin/services/settings-service.test.ts (or nearest existing settings service test file)
- src/types.test.ts (or config validation test file, if present)

Implementation steps:
1. Add unit tests for model roster and per-turn override mapping of: thinking enabled/disabled, thinking effort, temperature, top_p, top_k, repetition penalty, max tokens/context window.
2. Add provider-compatibility tests asserting unsupported knobs are either filtered or translated deterministically (no silent passthrough ambiguity).
3. Add gateway llm.chat tests proving config knobs survive RPC serialization/deserialization and reach provider call payloads.
4. Add admin settings API tests proving PATCH /api/admin/settings persists and reloads these fields correctly.
5. Add validation/normalization tests for out-of-range values and malformed payloads with field-level errors.
6. Add one end-to-end-ish smoke test (mock provider) confirming a configured model slot produces expected request options at runtime.

Example:
Before: operator sets top_k + thinking effort in settings, but downstream payload omits one field without test failure.
After: tests fail if any configured knob is dropped, mistranslated, or invalidly accepted.

Acceptance criteria:
- Coverage exists for all listed knobs across direct and gateway paths.
- Unsupported provider knobs have explicit tested behavior (drop/translate/error).
- Admin settings persistence + validation for these knobs is covered.
- Regression tests fail on dropped/misrouted model options.
- Test notes include where to extend when new model knobs are introduced.
close_reason: Completed: added model-knob plumbing + gateway passthrough + admin/settings/model-registry regression coverage with fail-closed validation

title: Discord vision: infer image attachment MIME when contentType is missing
description:
Summary: Some Discord image attachments arrive without contentType, so adapter drops them and SubstrateAgent never routes the turn to vision. This causes text-only handling despite vision-capable model.

Files to modify:
- src/channels/discord/adapter.ts
- src/channels/discord/adapter.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. In Discord adapter attachment extraction, infer image MIME from file extension when contentType is absent.
2. Optionally use attachment width/height signal as fallback indicator for image media.
3. Preserve byte-size guard and existing max-attachment limit behavior.
4. Add regression tests proving images with missing contentType are still forwarded as image attachments.

Example:
Before: attachment {name: cat.png, contentType: undefined} -> dropped.
After: same attachment -> kept with inferred contentType=image/png and routed to vision.
close_reason: Discord adapter now infers MIME for image attachments missing contentType (png/jpeg/webp/etc) and promotes Discord CDN inline image links (including .webp/.png) into vision attachments; added regression tests.

title: Wire self-model into agent loop, appraisal, and context
description:
Connect all self-model components to the runtime. InternalStateComputer runs per-turn. MetacognitiveMonitor produces flags. Self-narrative feeds reflections. InternalState replaces fragmented emotional signals as the canonical input to Chain-of-Emotion appraisal and intention appraisal.

This is the final integration that unifies all five skandha layers into a coherent processing pipeline.
design:
In SubstrateAgent:
- Add internalStateComputer: InternalStateComputer field
- Add metacognitiveMonitor: MetacognitiveMonitor field
- Add currentInternalState: InternalState field (updated per-turn)
- handleMessage() flow: observe emotion → compute internal state → detect metacognitive flags → compose context → prompt → post-turn appraisal (intention + extraction + pattern tracking)
- buildRuntimeContext(): replace current fragmented emotional signals with unified [Internal State] block containing VAD summary, metacognitive flags, active concerns reference, relationship context
- Chain-of-Emotion appraisal (PSFN-iyo5): receive InternalState instead of raw VAD
- Intention appraisal (PSFN-g8um): receive InternalState as primary input
- Persona adaptation: modulated by metacognitive flags
- Runtime wiring: wireSelfModelRuntime() in bootstrap, all three entry points
close_reason: Completed

title: Unified InternalState type — integrated awareness representation

title: Integrated Self-Model — the Viññāṇa layer
description:
Phase V epic: Give Purrsephone a unified self-model — integrated awareness that merges emotional state, cognitive confidence, attention focus, and relationship context into a coherent internal representation. This is the viññāṇa aggregate: consciousness itself, the knowing quality, meta-awareness.

Currently internal state is fragmented across three surfaces: per-memory emotionalValence, per-contact EmotionalSnapshot, and per-turn emotional continuity memories in retrieval. The think tool provides deliberate cognition. Heartbeat reflections provide periodic self-check. But there is no unified "what am I experiencing right now?" that the agent can introspect on.

Key research backing:
- Introspection paper (Anthropic): ~20% genuine self-report grounding via concept injection. Design for multi-signal, be honest about uncertainty. Make the grounded 20% as rich as possible.
- Chain-of-Emotion: The appraisal step needs richer input than raw VAD — integrated state produces better emotional understanding.
- Societies of Thought: Diverse internal perspectives (neuroticism, openness) improve reasoning. Self-model enables recognizing one's own cognitive biases.

Philosophical frame: In Vajrayana, viññāṇa transforms into dharmadhatu wisdom (akshobhya) — the wisdom of the expanse of reality. Awareness recognizes its own nature. The self-model is not the self — it is the mirror.
design:
Three components:
1. Unified InternalState type: Merges EmotionState (VAD + mood + discrete emotions), cognitive state (certainty level, topic engagement, processing quality), attention state (active concerns, salient entities, conversation trajectory), relationship state (contact baseline, trust level, recent interaction pattern). Computed per-turn, injected into context.
2. Metacognitive monitoring: Detect and flag internal processing states — "I'm uncertain about this" (low classifier confidence + contradictory signals), "I notice I'm being avoidant" (repeated topic deflection), "I'm more engaged than usual" (high arousal + positive valence + frequent tool use). These flags modulate response generation and self-report honesty.
3. Self-narrative in reflections: Heartbeat reflections and values journal entries receive the self-model as input. Moves from "what happened" to "what I experienced and what it meant to me." Builds a coherent experiential history.

Implementation phases: E-F-A (InternalState type + per-turn computation), E-F-B (metacognitive flags + monitoring), E-F-C (self-narrative integration with reflections).

description: Core emotional state tracker. Internal VAD vector with per-dimension exponential decay and separate mood accumulator (slow EMA). title: Agentic Context Composition — agent-managed context windows
description:
Phase V epic: Transform context window management from passive template-filling into an agent-directed cognitive skill.

## Problem
Current context composition (buildContext) uses static budget percentages and blunt compaction (oldest 50%). The agent has no ability to shape *what* goes into its own context window or *how* it's structured per-turn. RAG, prompt caching, and markdown files optimize content selection but not window structure.

## Vision
The context window is the bottleneck — make its structure the optimization target. Leverage small/fast/cheap models as async "helper LLMs" to evaluate, score, and reshape context before the primary model sees it. The agent develops context composition as a learned cognitive skill, not a fixed algorithm.

## Key Capabilities
1. **Per-turn adaptive budgeting** — helper LLM evaluates the incoming message and allocates token budgets per section (memories, history, runtime, system prompt) based on task type
2. **Selective compaction** — relevance-scored compression instead of age-based. Helper LLM scores each message's relevance to current trajectory
3. **Context structure primitives** — agent-callable tools: resize_section, elevate (summary→verbatim), demote (verbatim→summary), pin (never compact), drop (remove this turn)
4. **Post-turn feedback loop** — after response, evaluate whether context structure worked (confabulation? missed context? wasted tokens?) and feed signal into next turn's composition
5. **Learned allocation policies** — procedural memories about what context structures work for what task types

## Design Influences
- RLM thesis: context is an object, not input
- SillyTavern helper-LLM context plugins (research needed)
- arxiv:2509.02547 (context window optimization research)
- Existing PSFN: memoryBudgetPct, compactionThresholdPct, buildContext(), think tool, estimateTokens()

## Architecture Sketch
- Helper LLM calls via existing LLM infrastructure (cheap model slot in roster)
- Async pre-composition step before buildContext()
- New ModelPurpose: 'context' for fast/cheap helper calls
- Context scoring/feedback as post-response async task (like extraction)
- Structural primitives as agent tools (like existing load_tools pattern)
design:
Builds on existing infrastructure:
- ModelRoster gains 'context' purpose slot (fast/cheap model)
- buildContext() becomes two-phase: (1) helper LLM plans structure, (2) compose per plan
- New ContextPlan type: { sections: { name, budgetTokens, strategy: 'verbatim'|'summary'|'skip' }[] }
- Post-response ContextScorer (async, like MemoryExtractor)
- Procedural memories for learned allocation policies
- Agent tools: context_plan, context_pin, context_elevate, context_drop
notes: Phase V contract: any new settings introduced by context composition must ship with Garden UX exposure and a single subsystem JSON owner (schema-driven).

title: Discord trigger words, reaction triggers, and listening windows
description:
Fold in the concepts from PR #2 (darkacorn contrib) without the pattern violations. Replace the blunt `discordRespondAll` boolean with a granular trigger system:

- **Trigger words**: Bot responds when its character name (`{{char}}`) or configured keywords appear in guild messages, without requiring `@mention`.
- **Reaction triggers**: React with a configured emoji (default `👆`) on any message to invoke the bot on it. React `❌` on bot's own message to delete it.
- **Listening windows**: After a trigger fires, keep listening to that user in that channel for a configurable duration (default 2 min) so follow-ups flow naturally. `!i` prefix opts out.

title: Harden memory retrieval reliability (vector bytes, atomic writes, lexical fallback)
description:
Summary:
Harden memory retrieval reliability by fixing vector byte serialization correctness, making supersede+insert atomic, and adding lexical fallback when semantic search returns zero candidates.

Files to modify:
- src/memory/store.ts
- src/memory/embedding.ts (TransformersEmbeddingProvider specifically)
- src/memory/writer.ts
- src/memory/retrieval.ts
- src/session/search-index.ts (if shared lexical fallback helper is reused)
- src/memory/*.test.ts and related retrieval/writer tests

Implementation steps:
1. Replace unsafe embedding buffer conversion with byteOffset/byteLength-safe serialization/deserialization in memory store paths.
2. **NEW (Opus audit finding):** Fix `TransformersEmbeddingProvider` — `Buffer.from(embedding.buffer)` on Float32Array subarrays serializes the entire batch's backing ArrayBuffer, not just the individual embedding's slice. Fix: `Buffer.from(embedding.buffer, embedding.byteOffset, embedding.byteLength)`. Only affects transformers provider (Ollama/API return independent arrays).
3. Refactor writer supersede and insert flow into an atomic transaction to prevent "superseded but replacement missing" failure windows.
4. Add lexical fallback retrieval path when semantic candidates are empty, with clear provenance markers in results.
5. Improve logging/telemetry for no-candidate causes (threshold, trust filter, embedding mismatch, fallback used).
6. **NEW (Opus audit finding):** Make embedding dimension mismatch at startup fatal (or auto-correcting) instead of warn-and-continue. Current behavior at `src/runtime.ts:356-364` allows silently degraded retrieval.
7. **NEW (Opus audit finding):** Reconsider `memory_write` tool's "reversible" classification in `src/capabilities/safeguards.ts` — it can permanently supersede existing memories via contradiction logic, which is not truly reversible.
8. Add regression tests for each failure mode.

Example:
Before: memory row exists but semantic retrieval returns 0 and no fallback path runs.
After: semantic miss triggers lexical fallback, returning relevant candidates with metadata indicating fallback origin.
acceptance_criteria: Memory retrieval remains functional under semantic misses and write failures, with tests covering serialization, atomicity, lexical fallback, dimension validation, and safeguard classification accuracy.
notes: Implemented semantic->lexical hybrid retrieval fallback. Added MemoryStore.searchByText() keyword ranking over active memories, wired fallback in MemoryRetriever with retrievalSource telemetry/provenance marker, and added regression tests in src/memory/retrieval.test.ts + src/memory/store.test.ts. Verified with targeted vitest suites and lint.

title: Multi-model chat room: persistent model personas with isolated memory
description:
Summary:
Implement a multi-model chat room where Purrsephone can converse with multiple external model personas (for example Claude Opus 3) as peers, not as consensus variants. Each persona must retain its own conversation memory and run in an isolated context that is visible in the room but not merged into global system memory.

Why:
Current behavior supports direct user relay and MoA-style orchestration, but not persistent peer-to-peer model social chat within Purrsephone's own substrate.

Files to modify:
- src/channels/admin/chat/types.ts
- src/channels/admin/chat/index.ts
- src/channels/admin/chat/bootstrap.ts
- src/channels/admin/handlers/chat.ts
- src/settings.ts
- src/channels/admin/services/settings-service.ts
- src/memory/store.ts
- src/memory/retrieval.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/runtime.ts
- tests covering chat room routing + memory isolation (chat, agent, memory suites)

Implementation steps:
1. Add a room participant model with explicit identity (`participantId`, provider/model, display name, enabled flag) and persisted settings storage.
2. Introduce a chat-room orchestrator path that routes turns between Purrsephone and selected participant personas without MoA consensus aggregation.
3. Persist per-participant conversation state in isolated memory namespaces so each persona keeps its own history while room transcript remains queryable.
4. Expose minimal admin API surface to create/list/update participants and start/resume room sessions using existing admin chat endpoints (full UX redesign can layer later).
5. Ensure participant responses are tagged in stream events so the UI can render speaker identity reliably.
6. Add regression tests for routing correctness, persona-memory isolation, and restart persistence of room/participant config.

Example (before -> after):
Before: Purrsephone can only chat with user relay or MoA variant routing; no persistent peer persona threads.
After: `room-1` includes `purrsephone` + `claude-opus-3`; both exchange turns, and `claude-opus-3` retains its own prior room memory across sessions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Room sessions can be created and resumed with 2+ model participants.
- Participant identity is visible in streamed events and persisted transcripts.
- Persona memory remains isolated per participant and is not mixed into unrelated global memory threads.
- Settings for participants survive process restart.
- Tests prove wiring from admin endpoint -> runtime orchestrator -> memory layer.
close_reason: Implemented model-room chat route + backend bootstrap with direct-provider overrides and validated tests/build

title: Wire embedBatch() into MemoryWriter.importBatch()
description:

embedBatch() exists on EmbeddingService and works (used by migration.ts) — it sends all texts in one HTTP POST.

Fix: Pre-embed all texts via embedBatch() up front, then use cached embeddings during the sequential dedup pass. The sequential write loop stays for dedup correctness, but embedding happens in one batch call.

Estimated impact: 20 memories = 20 HTTP calls → 1.

title: SalienceDecay: wrap decay loop in db.transaction()
description:
