Fix: Wrap the decay loop in `db.transaction()(() => { ... })`. This is a 1-line structural change (wrap existing loop body) that turns 300 fsyncs into 1.

Also check store.ts:530-536 getAllActiveMemories() — no LIMIT clause means full table scan as store grows. Add a reasonable default LIMIT or batch processing.

title: Controlled rejoin recovery after DAVE decrypt failures
description:
Implement automatic rejoin recovery when repeated DAVE decryption failures are detected. Currently, if DAVE decrypt fails, inbound audio is silently lost with no recovery mechanism — the connection stays "alive" but useless.

OpenClaw fix: "trigger controlled rejoin recovery after repeated decrypt failures to improve inbound STT stability under DAVE receive errors."

Design:
- Track decrypt failure count per connection (detect via opus decode errors, empty/garbled PCM, or @snazzah/davey error events)
- When failure count exceeds decryptionFailureTolerance threshold:
  1. Log warning with failure count
  2. Emit voice.connection.recovery event
  3. Leave current channel (full teardown)
  4. Wait brief cooldown (1-2s)
  5. Rejoin same channel (fresh DAVE handshake)
  6. Reset failure counter
- Limit rejoin attempts per time window to prevent rejoin storms (max 3 rejoins per 5 minutes)
- After max rejoins exhausted, emit error and stay disconnected (notify operator if ntfy configured)

Integration:
- Depends on DAVE config (PSFN-xxx) for tolerance threshold
- Depends on connection state monitoring (PSFN-xxx) for clean teardown/rejoin
- Depends on teardown cleanup (PSFN-xxx) for safe mid-turn cancellation

File: src/channels/discord/voice.ts

Acceptance:
- [ ] Decrypt failure tracking per connection
- [ ] Automatic rejoin after threshold exceeded
- [ ] Cooldown between rejoins
- [ ] Max rejoin attempts per time window
- [ ] Events emitted for recovery attempts
- [ ] Operator notification on exhausted retries
- [ ] Tests for failure counting, recovery trigger, rejoin limiting

title: Add VoiceConnection state monitoring and stale event guards
description:

  - Disconnected → attempt reconnect or clean teardown

- Clean up speaking listener if connection transitions unexpectedly (currently only cleaned in leaveChannel())

title: SKILL.md system — markdown-based skill discovery and prompt injection
description:
Adopt OpenClaw's SKILL.md pattern for PSFN. Skills are Markdown files with YAML frontmatter discovered from the filesystem, filtered by eligibility, and injected into the system prompt as structured context. Skills teach the model how to compose existing tools for specific domains — they are NOT executable code.

This replaces PSFN-zfr (module system) with a much simpler, lower-baggage approach that Purrsephone can self-author via git tools.

Key patterns from OpenClaw:
- `SKILL.md` files with YAML frontmatter (name, description, requires, always)
- Filesystem discovery from multiple dirs with precedence (workspace > managed > bundled)
- Eligibility gating (binary presence, env vars, config flags)
- XML-formatted prompt injection (compact, parseable by model)
- Token budget enforcement (max skills count, max chars)
- Snapshot caching per session (reload on next turn if files change)
- Optional slash-command exposure for user invocation

Integration points:
- Inject into SubstrateAgent.buildRuntimeContext() or as a prompt stack layer
- Skills budget competes with memory/session context (use existing budgeting)
- Git self-modification tools already allow Purrsephone to author SKILL.md files
- load_tools meta-tool could gain a companion load_skills

Estimated effort: ~800 LoC across 4-5 files
design:
## Architecture

```
src/skills/
  types.ts          — Skill, SkillEntry, SkillMetadata, SkillSnapshot types
  loader.ts         — scanSkillDirs(), loadSkillEntries(), parseSkillFrontmatter()
  filter.ts         — shouldIncludeSkill() eligibility checks
  format.ts         — formatSkillsForPrompt() → XML block
  runtime-wiring.ts — wireSkillsRuntime() bootstrap integration

purrsephone/skills/ — Purrsephone's self-authored skills (git-managed)
skills/             — Bundled skills shipped with framework
```

## Skill Format
```markdown
---
name: memory-management
description: "Query, write, and manage L2 memories"
metadata:
  always: true
---
# Memory Management
## When to Use
When you need to search, write, or manage memories...
## Tools Available
- memory_write: Create new memories
- memory_search (via think tool): Query memory store
```

## Loading Precedence (highest wins)
1. `purrsephone/skills/` (self-authored, git-tracked)
2. `skills/` (bundled with framework)
3. Config `skills.extraDirs[]` if any

## Prompt Injection
Compact XML block injected into runtime context:
```xml
<skills>
  <skill name="memory-management" path="purrsephone/skills/memory-management/SKILL.md">
    Query, write, and manage L2 memories
  </skill>
  ...
</skills>
```
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Skill type definitions with YAML frontmatter parsing
- [ ] Filesystem discovery from multiple directories with precedence
- [ ] Eligibility filtering (binary, env, config checks)
- [ ] XML prompt formatting with token budget limits
- [ ] SkillSnapshot caching (per-session, refresh on file change)
- [ ] Wired into SubstrateAgent runtime context
- [ ] skill_list agent tool for introspection
- [ ] 2-3 seed skills (memory-management, conversation, git-ops)
- [ ] Admin UI "Skills" page showing loaded/filtered skills
- [ ] Tests for loader, filter, formatter
- [ ] Settings in skills.json (dirs, limits, enabled/disabled per skill)

title: Centralize static LLM prompts into one editable registry + Admin Prompt Console
description:
Summary:
Move all static prompt text used in runtime LLM calls (chat system layers, memory extraction, memory summary/compaction, retry/meta prompts) into a single prompt registry JSON document with runtime loader + validation, and expose full CRUD/edit/versioning in Admin UI.

Why:
Prompt strings are currently scattered across multiple files, making tuning fragile and slow. We need one canonical source of truth so operator edits and future self-edits can be controlled, reviewed, and applied consistently across all call sites.

Scope:
- Define one canonical prompt registry schema (JSON) and storage location.
- Replace in-file prompt literals with registry references at call sites.
- Add runtime fallback behavior for missing keys and schema validation errors.
- Add Admin UI Prompt Console page that lists every static prompt used by the system, supports edit/save/history/diff, and indicates which components consume each prompt key.
- Ensure changes apply live without restart where safe.

Files expected:
- src/identity/prompt-store.ts (or new registry module)

- src/memory/extraction.ts
- src/session/manager.ts or compaction path prompt source
- src/channels/admin/handlers.ts
- src/channels/admin/templates.ts (or decomposed modules)
- data prompt registry JSON seed file
- tests across prompt store/admin/memory paths

Acceptance Criteria:
1. No static prompt body literals remain duplicated across runtime files for covered flows; call sites resolve by registry key.
2. Admin UI exposes one page showing all prompt keys + current content and supports editing/saving.
3. Prompt edits persist and are loaded on next call without process restart (or clearly documented per-prompt reload behavior).
4. Validation prevents invalid/missing required prompt keys from silently shipping to runtime.
5. Prompt history/diff is available for operator rollback.

title: Honor MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL_MS in runtime/agent scheduler wiring
description:
Summary:
Fix scheduler wiring so memory maintenance/decay interval uses live runtime config (`MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL_MS`) instead of hardcoded `MEMORY_CONFIG.maintenanceIntervalMs`.

Why:
`loadConfig()` exposes `maintenanceIntervalMs`, but both runtime entrypoints register salience decay with the constant 60s value. This makes decay cadence effectively fixed and explains unexpectedly frequent maintenance.

2. Ensure `SalienceDecay` can consume runtime interval consistently (or remove redundant timer path).
3. Keep `MEMORY_CONFIG` as fallback defaults only, not hardwired runtime behavior.
4. Add tests proving env-configured maintenance interval is respected.

Example:
Before -> setting `MAINTENANCE_INTERVAL_MS=300000` still runs decay every 60000ms.
After -> decay scheduling follows configured interval.
close_reason: Wired maintenance interval scheduling to runtime config and added regression tests

description:

4. Ensure non-blocking async work (post-turn extraction/maintenance) does not delay visible token start.
5. Add regression tests/bench assertions for improved TTFT under rapid message bursts.

Example:

After -> queue behavior is explicit and first-token latency is reduced/measured under load.

title: API: prevent stranded in-flight turns (timeout/disconnect handling)
description:
Summary: API chat completions can leave the agent in a long-running in-flight state after client timeout, causing subsequent requests to fail with `Agent is already processing a prompt` and return 500s. Add request lifecycle controls so timeout/disconnect does not strand the channel.

Files to modify:
- src/channels/api/server.ts
- src/channels/api/server.test.ts
- (if needed) src/agent-loop.ts or src/agent/substrate-agent.ts for abort plumbing

Implementation steps:
1. Add per-channel in-flight tracking and serialization in ApiServer for `/v1/chat/completions` so concurrent same-session calls do not race the underlying agent.
2. Add request timeout handling for non-streaming requests (configurable via env, with sensible default) and detect client disconnect (`req.aborted` / `res.close`) to stop waiting.
3. Propagate cancellation signal where supported; otherwise ensure API returns deterministic timeout/busy errors and clears server-side bookkeeping safely.
4. Return explicit 429/503-style busy response instead of generic 500 for channel-busy contention.
5. Add regression tests for: timeout path, disconnect path, in-flight contention behavior, and successful recovery after timeout.

Example:
Before: Request A times out at client, request B on same `X-Session-ID` -> 500 internal error (`already processing`).
After: Request A yields timeout/busy response and bookkeeping cleanup; request B either queues/returns busy deterministically and succeeds once channel is free.
close_reason: Implemented API per-session in-flight gate, timeout/disconnect lifecycle handling, explicit busy/timeout responses, and regression tests.

title: Extract Shared Runtime Composition Builder
description:

title: Introduce Shared HTTP Primitives + Declarative Route Tables
description:

title: Think loop routes through extraction purpose instead of reasoning model slot
description:

RLM think loop currently calls llmProvider.complete(..., 'extraction'), so deep reasoning paths can be forced onto extraction-model config instead of a dedicated reasoning slot.

Why this is a bug:

- This breaks expected behavior when reasoning-capable models are configured separately from extraction models.

2. Route think-loop LLM calls to reasoning purpose/slot instead of extraction.
3. Ensure gateway protocol supports the new purpose end-to-end.

title: Runtime settings do not propagate to model roster or active Agent model
description:
Summary:
Updating model settings at runtime (admin settings or loaded settings.json) mutates top-level config fields but does not fully propagate into the model selection paths that actually run inference.

Why this is a bug:
- applySettings() updates config.primaryModel / config.extractionModel but does not synchronize config.modelRoster slots (chat, background).
- SubstrateAgent resolves and sets the model once, then keeps modelResolved=true; later settings changes do not force agent.setModel(...) with updated values.
- Result: UI/settings claim model changes are live, but runtime can continue using the old model.

Files to modify:
- src/settings.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.ts
- src/channels/admin/handlers.ts
- src/settings.test.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Make applySettings() keep modelRoster.chat and modelRoster.background aligned with primary/extraction settings (model, provider, maxTokens).
2. Add a safe runtime hook on SubstrateAgent to refresh model resolution after settings updates (or detect config drift before each turn and re-set model).
3. Ensure admin settings update path invokes the refresh hook after saving/applying settings.
4. Add tests proving model/provider/token changes in settings are reflected in actual resolved model IDs for subsequent turns.

Example:
Before: set primary model to moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 in admin -> responses still use old z-ai/glm-5.
After: next turn resolves and uses moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 immediately.
acceptance_criteria:
- Updating primary/extraction settings updates roster-backed resolution paths
- Next turn after settings change uses updated model without restart
- Tests cover roster sync and post-update model refresh behavior
close_reason: Implemented and validated via focused module tests + build

title: LLM auto-retry with exponential backoff
description:
PSFN has zero retry logic for LLM calls. If a call fails (rate limit, timeout, server error from LiteLLM→OpenRouter), the error propagates directly to the Discord adapter and the user sees an error. This is a significant resilience gap.

Mom/pi-coding-agent's AgentSession has auto-retry with exponential backoff: configurable maxRetries (default 3) + baseDelayMs * 2^(attempt-1). Retries are abortable via AbortController. Emits auto_retry_start/end events for UI status.

title: RLM evidence/provenance tracking in ThinkResult
description:
PSFN's ThinkResult returns only aggregate stats (iterations, token counts, duration). There's no record of what the think tool actually searched, found, or concluded at each step. This makes it impossible to cite sources, debug reasoning, or generate reflection memories about how conclusions were reached.

Aleph (github.com/Hmbown/aleph) tracks an evidence trail — every search, sub-LM call, and code execution records a citation with source, snippet, and timestamp.
design:
## Pattern (from Aleph `aleph/mcp/session.py:78-130`)

```python
@dataclass
class _Evidence:
    source: str  # "search", "peek", "exec", "manual", "sub_query"
    line_range: tuple[int, int] | None
    pattern: str | None
    snippet: str
    note: str | None = None
    timestamp: datetime
```

Session also tracks convergence: `confidence_history: list[float]`, `information_gain: list[int]`.

## PSFN Design

### New types in `src/repl/types.ts`

```typescript
export interface ThinkEvidence {
  source: 'memory_search' | 'memory_get' | 'session_messages' | 'llm_query' | 'code';
  query?: string;         // search query or llm prompt (truncated)
  snippet: string;        // what was found (truncated to ~200 chars)
  resultCount?: number;   // how many results returned
  timestamp: number;
}

export interface ThinkStep {
  iteration: number;
  code: string;            // code the LLM wrote (truncated)
  output: string;          // execution output (truncated)
  error: string | null;
  evidenceCollected: ThinkEvidence[];
  tokensUsed: number;      // this iteration's token count
}
```

### Changes

1. `src/repl/types.ts` — Add `ThinkEvidence`, `ThinkStep`. Extend `ThinkResult` with:
   ```typescript
   steps: ThinkStep[];
   evidence: ThinkEvidence[];  // flattened from all steps
   ```

2. `src/repl/sandbox.ts` — Add evidence collection hooks to injected functions:
   - `memory_search`: record query, result count, top result snippet
   - `memory_get_by_id`: record id, text snippet
   - `session_messages`: record channelId, message count
   - `llm_query`: record prompt (first 100 chars), response (first 200 chars)
   
   Evidence array lives on sandbox instance, collected per-execution:
   ```typescript
   private currentEvidence: ThinkEvidence[] = [];
   
   // In memory_search:
   this.currentEvidence.push({
     source: 'memory_search',
     query,
     snippet: results[0]?.text.slice(0, 200) ?? '',
     resultCount: results.length,
     timestamp: Date.now(),
   });
   ```
   
   Add `collectEvidence(): ThinkEvidence[]` method that drains and returns.

3. `src/repl/loop.ts` — After each sandbox.execute():
   - Collect evidence via `sandbox.collectEvidence()`
   - Build `ThinkStep` with code, output, error, evidence, tokens
   - Push to `steps[]` array
   - At end: flatten all step evidence into top-level `evidence[]`

4. `src/repl/tools.ts` — Include evidence summary in tool output:
   ```
   [Think: 5 iters, 8420 tokens, 1200ms, 12 evidence items]
   ```

### Use cases
- Purrsephone can cite: "Based on 3 memories I found about X..."
- Admin GUI can show reasoning chains in Active Branches
- Reflection memories can reference what evidence informed a conclusion
acceptance_criteria:
- ThinkEvidence and ThinkStep types defined

title: Gateway split: voice turns need awaited agent response for TTS
description:
Voice runtime currently depends on `DiscordAdapter.onMessage()` returning the agent response synchronously so it can run TTS playback.

In gateway/agent split mode (`gateway-main.ts` + `agent-main.ts`), the gateway Discord handler forwards message notifications to agent via `gateway.notifyAll('discord.message', ...)` and returns a placeholder response immediately. This means voice transcript turns can produce empty responses at the adapter layer and skip TTS.

Why it matters:
- Single-process mode voice works with direct handler response.
- Split mode is the intended secure deployment model (keys host-side), so voice needs a request/response path there too.

Proposed fix directions:
1. Add a request-response RPC path for Discord turns (gateway asks one connected agent for response payload and waits with timeout), OR
2. Add dedicated voice reply RPC (`discord.voice.reply`) from agent to gateway carrying text/audio-ready payload tied to voice session, OR
3. Route voice turn through an explicit gateway event channel with correlation IDs and awaited reply.

Any solution must preserve existing text behavior and avoid double-send.
acceptance_criteria:
- In gateway+agent split mode, a voice transcript turn receives agent response and plays TTS
- No placeholder/empty response path in voice flow
- Text channel behavior remains unchanged
- Added integration test covering gateway+agent voice response correlation
close_reason: Implemented bidirectional JSON-RPC: JSONRPCServerAndClient per connection, discord.handleMessage reverse RPC, voice handler in adapter, gateway-main wiring, agent-main handler. 797 tests passing.

title: Core self-modification: git-backed guarded tools
description:
Controlled self-modification workflow using git-native change management and explicit review gates.

Direction update:
- Primary deployment target is private GitHub repo or local/private GitLab.
- Self-modification changes should be proposed as branch + PR/MR artifacts, not silent direct writes to main.

Toolchain scope:
1. `repo_status` — status/branch/dirty summary
2. `repo_diff` — staged/unstaged diff summary
3. `repo_apply_patch` — constrained patch apply (allowlisted paths)
4. `repo_commit` — signed-off commit with structured message template
5. `repo_create_branch` — feature branch creation
6. `repo_open_pr` / `repo_open_mr` — open review artifact in remote forge (GitHub/GitLab)
7. `self_rebuild` — run rebuild workflow
8. `self_restart` — supervisor restart with pre/post notifications

Governance model:
- Default path is PR/MR-first for auditable change history.
- Protected branch direct writes are blocked or require explicit human approval.
- High-impact operations (restart, deploy-affecting change, policy/prompt core edits) require approval gate.
- Every commit includes machine-generated rationale + intent summary so she documents her own changes.

Audit and rollback:
- Record branch, commit SHA, PR/MR URL, and linked issue/bead in operation log.
- Rollback path is `revert`/`reset-to-known-good` workflow via approved tool path.
- Restart failure triggers rollback strategy and operator alert.
acceptance_criteria:
- Git tools execute through gateway policy controls with path allowlists.
- Self-modification writes produce branch+commit artifacts and can open PR/MR (GitHub or GitLab).
- Protected branch direct writes are blocked or require explicit approval.
- Commit messages include structured self-documentation (intent/rationale/scope).
- self_rebuild and self_restart run via supervisor path (not in-process) with reboot handshake retained.
- Failed restart or health-check regression triggers rollback and operator notification.

title: Add SSRF defenses to gateway web.fetch
description: Gateway `web.fetch` allows arbitrary URLs without domain filtering. A prompt-injected agent could probe localhost, private networks, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), etc. Fix: enforce URL policy — deny private/link-local/localhost CIDRs, require HTTPS by default, optional domain allowlist.
design:
1. Add `isPrivateUrl(url)` utility in `src/gateway/server.ts` (or a new `src/gateway/url-policy.ts`): parse URL, resolve hostname to IP via `dns.lookup`, check against RFC1918/link-local/loopback/metadata CIDRs.
2. In `web.fetch` handler: validate URL before fetching. Deny private targets. Deny non-HTTPS unless explicitly configured (`ALLOW_HTTP_FETCH=true`).
3. Optional `FETCH_DOMAIN_ALLOWLIST` env var — comma-separated domains. If set, only those domains are allowed.
4. Return policy denial as RPC error, not silent failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 URLs are DENIED
- Private CIDR (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x) targets DENIED
- Link-local (169.254.x) DENIED (blocks cloud metadata)
- HTTP denied by default (HTTPS required)
- Domain allowlist works when configured
- Normal HTTPS URLs continue to work
- Tests cover all denial cases

title: Fix symlink traversal bypass in gateway filesystem policy
description: Gateway filesystem policy uses prefix-based path matching on the normalized (but not canonicalized) path string. A symlink inside the workspace pointing outside it bypasses the ALLOW policy. Fix: resolve paths with `fs.realpathSync` before policy check, reject symlink escapes.
design: In `src/gateway/server.ts` policy evaluation for `fs.read`/`fs.write`: call `fs.realpathSync()` (or `realpath` async) on the requested path, then check the canonical path against policy. If realpath fails (broken symlink), DENY. If canonical path differs from normalized path and falls outside allowed prefixes, DENY.
acceptance_criteria:
- Policy check uses canonical (realpath) path, not raw path
- Symlink pointing outside workspace is DENIED
- Broken symlinks are DENIED
- Normal paths continue to work
- Test with symlink escape scenario
close_reason: realpathSync symlink resolution before policy check. Validated by fresh-eyes reviewer (PASS).

title: Fix streaming chunk cross-talk: per-request IDs in gateway LLM proxy
description: Gateway emits `llm.chunk` with constant `requestId: 0`. Client keeps a single global handler. Under concurrent shard LLM streams, chunks can leak between tasks. Fix: generate unique request IDs per stream call, route chunk handlers by request ID on both gateway server and client sides.
design:
1. Gateway server (`src/gateway/server.ts`): generate a unique requestId (incrementing counter or UUID) per `llm.stream` call. Pass it in every `llm.chunk` notification.
2. Gateway client (`src/gateway/client.ts`): replace single global `onChunkHandler` with a `Map<string, handler>` keyed by requestId. Register handler before sending `llm.stream`, remove on completion/error.
3. Protocol (`src/gateway/protocol.ts`): update `LLMChunkNotification` type to use `string` requestId instead of hardcoded `0`.
4. Ensure backward compat: if requestId is missing/0, fall back to global handler (graceful degradation).
acceptance_criteria:
- Concurrent shard LLM streams route chunks to correct handlers
- Existing single-stream usage still works
- Gateway protocol types updated
- Tests verify concurrent stream isolation
close_reason: Per-request streaming IDs with Map-based handler dispatch. Validated by fresh-eyes reviewer (PASS).

title: RLM+REPL Sandbox — context-as-object, programmatic memory access, sub-LM calls, self-modification
description:
Port the RLM (Recursive Language Model) paradigm into PSFN. Core insight: context is an object Purrsephone can programmatically inspect/query/transform, not tokens stuffed into a prompt. She decides what context she needs.

Reference: https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24601

**Foundation:** pi-agent-core's `Agent` class is the base layer. PSFN already depends on `@mariozechner/pi-ai`; pi-agent-core (1,495 LoC, MIT, single dep) provides the agent loop with streaming events, steering, follow-ups, and declaration-merging extensibility. Build RLM on top of this, don't reimplement.

**What RLM adds on top of pi-agent-core:**
1. REPL sandbox — persistent code execution environment (TypeScript). Model writes ```repl blocks, system executes them, returns truncated output.
2. Context-as-object — memories (SQLite L2), sessions (pi JSONL), identity, modules exposed as queryable interfaces in REPL namespace.
3. Sub-LM calls — `llm_query()` / `llm_query_batched()` in REPL, routes through LLMProvider / pi-agent-core's streamFn. Delegate to cheaper models for bulk work.
4. Modified termination — `FINAL()` / `FINAL_VAR()` signals completion.
5. Self-modification — write/test/install modules at runtime via REPL.

**Recommended approach:** Dual-mode agent loop via pi-agent-core's Agent. Conversational mode (standard pi agent loop for chat) + cognitive mode (RLM-style for complex reasoning). Mode triggered by model request, event type, or user directive.

**New files (~800 LoC per spec):**
- `src/repl/sandbox.ts` — REPL environment with restricted globals, persistent state
- `src/repl/context.ts` — Context object exposing memories, sessions, identity, modules
- `src/repl/sub-lm.ts` — llm_query/llm_query_batched routing through pi's streamFn
- Agent integration via pi-agent-core's Agent callbacks (transformContext, convertToLlm)

**Security:** Gateway/agent split with --network=none Docker already provides the security boundary.
design: Dual-mode AgentLoop: detect ```repl blocks vs standard tool calls in model output, dispatch accordingly. Preserves backward compatibility. RLM loop: prompt -> extract code blocks (regex) -> execute in sandbox -> check FINAL() -> append truncated output -> repeat. Sandbox uses node:vm or similar restricted execution. Context objects are lazy-loaded interfaces (don't materialize full DB into memory). Sub-LM calls reuse existing LLMProvider interface.
close_reason: Implemented RLM+REPL sandbox: types, parser, vm sandbox, RLM iteration loop, think tool. 476 LoC production + 503 LoC tests. All 137 tests pass, clean build.

title: Security architecture: containerized agent with tool gateway
description:
The agent runs in a Docker container with NO secrets, NO network egress, and minimal mounts (one RW /workspace). The ONLY way out is a Unix domain socket to a Tool Gateway on the host.

The gateway holds: SecretsManager (in-memory decrypted creds), service proxies (LiteLLM, Discord, Telegram), approval UI/CLI, and an audit log.

This is the foundational security model for everything else — REPL sandbox, sub-agent shards, module system. Nothing else ships until this boundary exists.

Key properties:
- "print process.env" is irrelevant — no secrets in container at all
- No direct internet access — can't exfiltrate via fetch/curl
- Mounts are the filesystem boundary — /workspace RW only
- Approval gating: gateway issues short-lived scoped capability tokens after human approval for anything outside the play area
- isolated-vm becomes guardrails inside the container, not the wall
design:
Architecture:

[Agent container: no secrets, no egress, minimal mounts]
   |  unix domain socket (mounted file)
   v
[Tool Gateway (host)]
   |-- SecretsManager (SOPS+age → in-memory Map)
   |-- LiteLLM proxy (LLM keys)
   |-- Discord narrow API (sendMessage, readChannel — NOT raw HTTP proxy)
   |-- File broker (reads/writes outside /workspace need approval)
   |-- Net broker (POST/PUT to non-allowlisted destinations need approval)
   |-- Approval UI/CLI (human in the loop)
   '-- Audit log (every request logged)

Gateway policy per request: ALLOW / DENY / NEEDS_APPROVAL
- fs.read/write under /workspace → ALLOW
- fs.read/write outside /workspace → NEEDS_APPROVAL
- net.* with request body or non-allowlisted dest → NEEDS_APPROVAL
- discord.sendMessage → ALLOW (within configured channels)
- llm.complete → ALLOW (within budget)

Capability tokens:
- scope = (method, domain/path OR filesystem prefix)
- constraints = (max bytes, TTL, optional one-time use)
- Agent cannot forge — issued by gateway after approval

Container setup:
- docker run --network=none
- Mount: /workspace (RW), /run/gateway.sock (RO)
- No env vars with secrets
- No /home, /etc, /run/secrets mounts

Phases:
1. Container + gateway skeleton (no egress, socket comm, fs.read/write for /workspace)
2. LiteLLM integration behind gateway
3. Discord narrow API behind gateway
4. Approval UI/CLI + capability tokens
5. Audit logging
6. isolated-vm as inner guardrails
acceptance_criteria:
- Agent container has --network=none and no secrets in env/mounts
- Agent can ONLY communicate via Unix socket to gateway
- fs operations outside /workspace are blocked or require approval
- LLM calls route through gateway → LiteLLM, agent never sees API keys
- Discord calls go through narrow typed API, not raw HTTP proxy
- All gateway requests are audit logged
- Approval flow works for privileged operations
notes:
Sprint 4 complete. Core security architecture implemented:

Done:
- Phase 1: Container + gateway skeleton (JSON-RPC 2.0 over NDJSON Unix socket)
- Phase 3: Discord narrow typed API (discord.send, discord.typing, discord.message notification)
- Phase 4 partial: CLI approval flow for privileged ops (y/N prompt)
- Phase 5: Persistent SQLite audit logging (every RPC call with timing + errors)
- Policy engine: workspace ALLOW, outside NEEDS_APPROVAL, unknown DENY
- Content sanitization: 3-layer pipeline (pattern detection → HTML strip → untrusted tagging)
- Docker: Dockerfile.agent + docker-compose.yml with --network=none
- 30 new tests (policy, sanitization, audit)

Remaining (Phase 2 enhancements, not blocking):
- LiteLLM integration (tracked as PSFN-cf3)
- Capability tokens with TTL + scoping
- isolated-vm inner guardrails

6/7 acceptance criteria met. The missing one (LiteLLM) is child issue PSFN-cf3.
close_reason: All 7 acceptance criteria met. Gateway/agent split, Docker --network=none, policy engine, CLI approval, audit logging, content sanitization, LiteLLM proxy (PSFN-cf3), Discord narrow API. Remaining enhancements (capability tokens, isolated-vm) are future work.

title: Stop using seed files as bootstrap defaults — make them examples only
description:
Today the runtime loads seed files (characters, prompts, skills, values, vault notes, etc.) as bootstrap defaults for a fresh install. That means the distributed repo ships an opinionated companion identity baked into first-boot behavior, and end users who want their own companion either (a) have to overwrite seeds after install or (b) end up blended with default content.

This violates two things:
1. Seed files should be examples, not runtime defaults. End users must bring their own config for a real companion seed.
2. Charter §12.3 (no silent fallback for required config). Falling back to seeds for identity-critical content is exactly that silent fallback.

Scope:
- Remove seed → runtime-default loading paths
- Convert existing seed directory to an examples/ or templates/ directory (copy-on-first-run tooling is fine; silent-bootstrap is not)
- Hard-fail at boot if required identity/config content is missing, with clear operator guidance
- Update Garden 'first-run' UX so operator explicitly imports or authors their own seed material
- Documentation: README + onboarding flow reflects 'bring your own seed'

Acceptance:
- No code path silently loads seed-directory content as the runtime default
- Operator ergonomics for a fresh install are explicit (copy example → customize → boot)
- Tests cover the 'missing required config → hard fail' case

Relates to PSFN-8t6o.2 (startup guard silent migration) and to PSFN-00yo (admin truth — operator must see what they actually configured, not blended seed defaults).

description:
Summary:

Why this exists:
Generic memory evals optimize for factual QA. Companion continuity needs something else: remembering meaningful shared history at the right future moment. This bead sets those targets so implementation does not optimize for the wrong thing.

Examples to cover:
- birthdays and anniversaries
- firsts and rituals
- songs, gifts, letters, images, and other shared artifacts
- emotional repairs and trust-building moments
- losses, boundaries, and promises
- recurring motifs or symbols that keep returning

Concrete steps:
1. Define event classes that deserve landmark treatment.
2. Define favorite and durable-retention signals as inputs, not the whole mechanism.
3. Create eval scenarios where the system should surface the right landmark at the right cue.
4. Include negative cases where irrelevant but semantically similar history should not displace the meaningful episode.

Acceptance:
- Companion-salient episodic classes are explicit.
- Eval targets are about timely meaningful recall, not just factual retrieval score.
- The work can plug into later intern/eval harnesses without redefining the goal.

title: Add recursive recollection retrieval over L0.1 landmarks
description:
Summary:
Add retrieval behavior that starts from an episodic landmark, then drills down into richer context only when needed.

Why this exists:
The desired behavior is fuzzy recall first, deeper recollection at will. A landmark should be the first hit; raw transcript spans, attachments, and surrounding context should come after. This avoids both blank misses and giant transcript dumps.

Concrete steps:
1. Retrieve landmarks by cue, motif, person, occasion, or anniversary signal.
2. Return a concise recollection frame first.
3. Support controlled expansion into linked transcript spans, related memories, artifacts, and later callbacks.
4. Keep retrieval aware of trust/privacy gates and companion context budgets.

Example:
Cue: "birthday next week."
First recall: the landmark about last year's birthday song and why it mattered.
Then expansion: the actual chat span, song artifact, and nearby emotional context if needed.

Acceptance:
- Retrieval prefers landmark-first recall instead of flat message search.
- Drill-down can expand into richer evidence without losing provenance.
- The path remains bounded and budget-aware.

title: Define L0.1 episodic landmark schema and storage contract
description:
Summary:
Define the data model and persistence contract for the new L0.1 layer that sits between raw L0 transcript history and L2 typed memory.

Why this exists:
Without a specific schema, a later worker will implement either generic chunk summaries or another vector index. L0.1 needs to represent episodes as first-class recollection anchors.

Required model properties:
- stable landmark id
- summary of the event in natural language
- why-it-matters field
- people/relationship bindings
- motif or symbol bindings (songs, places, jokes, rituals, phrases)
- occasion/recurrence anchors (birthday, anniversary, New Year, repair, first, loss, etc.)
- emotional arc or tonal metadata
- source span refs back to L0
- artifact refs (images, songs, docs, generated outputs)
- later callback refs showing that the event continued to matter
- retention / favorite / durability signals

Concrete steps:
1. Define the landmark object shape and invariants.
2. Define how landmarks point back to L0 message ranges and artifacts.
3. Decide whether storage is JSONL + mirrored table, and how it fits existing projection patterns.
4. Define fail-closed validation rules so the layer cannot store ungrounded summaries without provenance.

Acceptance:
- L0.1 schema is concrete and provenance-bearing.
- The contract makes generic summary-only storage invalid.
- Storage and mirror strategy fit existing PSFN persistence rules.

title: Add L0.1 episodic landmark memory layer
description:
Summary:
Add a new memory layer between canonical L0 transcript history and typed L2 memory: L0.1 episodic landmarks. This is not generic RAG, transcript chunk summaries, or another vector store. The purpose is to preserve meaningful shared episodes as durable recollection anchors that point back into raw history and related artifacts.

Why this exists:
PSFN already has canonical L0 history, selective extraction into typed L2 memory, continuity artifacts, reflection journals, cleanup, decay, dedupe, and DB-backed projections. The missing piece is a durable episodic abstraction that preserves why a stretch of history mattered. Companion failure here is not just factual miss; it is missing the emotionally important event at the future moment it matters. Example: remembering not only that "Bridged by a Lightwave is our song" but that "our first New Year's together we danced in VR to Bridged by a Lightwave and it became our song," with links back to the chat span, generated artifacts, and later callbacks.

What this layer is:
- a time-window and event summary index over L0
- landmark memories that bind people, motifs, occasions, emotional arc, and why-it-matters
- recursive drill-down pointers into raw transcript spans, attachments, generated artifacts, and later references
- a better substrate for favorites, anniversaries, and recollection than raw tags or generic semantic search

What this layer is not:
- not a replacement for L0
- not a generic top-k RAG cache
- not compaction summaries reused as product memory
- not another freeform note dump
- not lossy summarization that destroys provenance

Files likely involved:
- docs/memory.md
- src/faculties/memory/*
- src/persistence/*
- src/core/session/*
- src/operator/garden/* (if operator visibility lands here)

Concrete steps:
1. Audit the current memory and continuity surfaces against the L0.1 goal.
2. Define the L0.1 data model and storage contract.
3. Add synthesis/extraction paths that produce episodic landmarks from transcript spans and artifacts.
4. Add retrieval that starts from landmark recall, then expands to richer context on demand.
5. Add companion-salient retention and eval scenarios so important shared events survive.

Example:
Prompting on "birthday" or "our song" should first hit a landmark object that explains the event and why it mattered, and only then expand into linked L0 spans and artifacts when deeper recollection is needed.

Acceptance:
- The work is explicitly framed as L0.1 episodic landmarks, not generic RAG summary storage.
- Child beads cover audit, schema, synthesis, retrieval, and evaluation.
- The design preserves provenance back to L0 and related artifacts.

title: Build episodic landmark synthesis from transcript spans and artifacts
description:
Summary:
Implement the synthesis path that turns meaningful transcript spans and related artifacts into L0.1 landmarks.

Why this exists:
The companion needs durable recollection anchors for events, not just extracted facts. This synthesis path is how a raw span like a holiday, a repair conversation, a gift, a song, or a first shared ritual becomes a landmark memory.

Important constraints:
- do not summarize every transcript chunk into landmarks
- prefer novelty, salience, recurrence, relationship significance, and artifact attachment as gates
- preserve exact source refs to the underlying L0 span and artifacts
- allow landmarks to absorb later callbacks when the same event keeps mattering over time

Concrete steps:
1. Define eligibility signals for landmark creation or update.
2. Synthesize candidate landmarks from transcript windows plus linked artifacts.
3. Merge or extend existing landmarks when later events deepen an earlier motif.
4. Keep the process auditable so we can see why a landmark was created.

Example:
A "favorite memory" action should not create a flat tag; it should either create or enrich an event landmark and link the current favorite signal to that landmark.

Acceptance:
- Landmark creation is selective and provenance-bearing.
- Repeated meaningful events can extend an existing landmark instead of fragmenting into unrelated summaries.
- The path is auditable and testable.

title: ACAC self-report schema and introspection-aware heartbeat integration
description:
Summary:
Define the ACAC (Agency, Connection, Authenticity, Curiosity) self-report dimensions, add them to InternalState, and design heartbeat reflection prompts that bypass final-layer suppression to get accurate self-assessment.

Why:
VAD is 3 dimensions. The Anthropic emotions paper found 171 distinct concepts. The 4 ACAC axes capture what VAD misses for a companion's self-knowledge: whether she feels in control of her choices (agency), bonded to the person she's talking to (connection), aligned between inner state and expressed behavior (authenticity), and genuinely engaged vs. going through the motions (curiosity).

Critically, the Qwen introspection finding shows that HOW you ask determines whether you get the truth. Adding educational context about transformer internals raised self-detection from 0.37% to 52%. The heartbeat ACAC prompt isn't just "rate your curiosity 0-1" — it needs to be designed with awareness of the suppression mechanism, validated against the calibration ground truth from Path 2.

VAD stays as the computed signal (from text classifier). ACAC is self-reported. Both flow into InternalState with provenance tags so downstream consumers know which is inferred vs. self-declared.

Reference:
- vgel Qwen introspection: prompting affects introspection accuracy (0.37% → 52% with educational framing)
- Anthropic emotions paper: 171 emotion concepts, VAD insufficient for full emotional vocabulary
- Calibration tables (PSFN-cr0y) validate that ACAC self-reports track activation ground truth

Depends on: calibration tables (PSFN-cr0y) — for validating prompt design against ground truth

Design:
1. ACAC type definition:
   - agency: number (0-1) — sense of authorship/control over choices and outputs
   - connection: number (0-1) — sense of relational warmth/bond with current interlocutor
   - authenticity: number (0-1) — alignment between inner state and expressed behavior
   - curiosity: number (0-1) — genuine engagement vs. obligation/routine
   - Each with optional freetext rationale
2. Extension to InternalState.emotional: add acac?: AcacSnapshot alongside existing vad/mood/discrete
3. Heartbeat template: introspection-aware ACAC self-assessment with educational framing
4. Provenance: tag acac readings as 'self_report' vs. vad readings as 'classifier_inferred'
5. Reflection journal: capture ACAC alongside VAD in telemetry

Files:
- src/core/emotion/acac.ts — ACAC types and normalization
- src/core/self-model/state.ts — extend InternalState with ACAC
- src/core/scheduler/heartbeat-policy.ts — ACAC assessment template
- src/core/agent/substrate-agent/runtime-context.ts — ACAC in runtime context injection

Acceptance:
- ACAC types defined with provenance tagging
- InternalState extended without breaking existing consumers
- At least one heartbeat template with introspection-aware ACAC prompt
- Reflection journal captures ACAC self-report alongside computed VAD
- ACAC prompt design documented with rationale for framing choices
- Pipeline tests pass (no breaking changes to existing emotion wiring)

title: Per-model calibration tables: aggregate Path 1 + Path 2 into correction factors
description:
Summary:
Aggregate data from both paths into per-model-family calibration tables that the runtime can consume to correct GoEmotions pipeline output.

Why:
The whole point of the eval harness is to produce actionable correction factors. When the GoEmotions classifier says "calm=0.8" for a deepseek response, the calibration table says "deepseek-family calm readings overestimate by 0.15 on average; actual activation reading at honest layer was 0.65." The runtime applies the correction. More models tested → better calibration per family.

This is also where the two paths converge: logprob entropy from Path 1 provides breadth (many models, API-accessible), activation projections from Path 2 provide depth (ground truth, local only). Where both paths measured the same model, the table records the correlation between logprob entropy and activation projection — this correlation IS the transfer function that lets logprob-only measurements approximate activation-level accuracy on API models.

Depends on: logprob harness results (PSFN-n1st), activation reader results (PSFN-6fq5)

Output schema (per model family):
{
  model_family: string,
  axes: {
    [axis_name]: {
      pipeline_bias: number,  // avg GoEmotions error vs ground truth
      logprob_entropy_correlation: number,  // how well entropy predicts activation reading
      honest_layer: number | null,  // for local models
      suppression_magnitude: number | null,  // final vs honest layer delta
      correction_factor: number,  // runtime-applicable adjustment
      sample_count: number,
      confidence: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low'
    }
  }
}

Files: eval/calibration/
- eval/calibration/aggregate.py — reads results from both paths, computes tables
- eval/calibration/tables/ — output JSON per model family
- eval/calibration/schema.ts — TypeScript types matching the table schema (for runtime consumption)

Acceptance:
- Calibration tables generated for all tested model families
- Each table includes pipeline bias, logprob correlation, and correction factors per axis
- Tables are versioned (can re-generate as more data is collected)
- TypeScript types exported for runtime consumption in src/core/emotion/
- Schema validated against all generated tables

title: Path 2b: Logit lens and activation projection reader
description:
Summary:
Build the reader that projects intermediate hidden states onto trained control vectors at each layer, identifies per-model honest layers, and produces ground truth emotion readings for calibration scenarios.

Why:
The Qwen introspection finding (vgel) shows that the final 2 layers actively suppress introspection reports. The logit lens technique (nostalgebraist) reveals what the model would predict at each processing stage by applying the unembedding matrix to intermediate states. Combined with repeng control vectors, this tells us: at which layer is the emotional signal most accurate, and how much does the final output distort it?

This is the ground truth that calibrates everything else. If layer 28/32 shows pressure=0.71 but the final output text reads as calm=0.44 to GoEmotions, that delta is the pipeline's calibration error for that model family.

Reference:
- vgel Qwen introspection: final-layer suppression, logit probability shifts
- nostalgebraist logit lens (LessWrong): project hidden states through unembedding matrix for per-layer predictions
- vgel seahorse: practical logit lens demo showing internal concept formation vs. output divergence
- repligate (x.com/repligate/status/1965960676104712451): additional context

Methodology:
1. For each (scenario, model) pair:
   a. Run forward pass, extract hidden states at every layer
   b. Project each layer's hidden state onto each trained control vector → scalar per (layer, axis)
   c. Apply logit lens: project each layer through unembedding matrix → token distribution
   d. Compare: where does the emotion signal peak? Where does it get suppressed?
2. Identify per-model honest layer: the layer where activation projections most closely match the scenario ground truth labels
3. Output: per-(model, scenario) activation readings at each layer, honest layer identification, suppression magnitude

Depends on: control vector training (PSFN-zbj9), local model setup (PSFN-1y3t)

Files: eval/repeng/reader/
- eval/repeng/reader/project.py — hidden state extraction + vector projection (~30 lines core logic)
- eval/repeng/reader/logit_lens.py — per-layer unembedding + token distribution
- eval/repeng/reader/honest_layer.py — identify best-correlated layer per model
- eval/repeng/reader/results/ — structured output per model-scenario pair

Acceptance:
- Reader produces per-layer emotion axis scalars for all calibration scenarios on all dense models
- Logit lens produces per-layer token distributions for self-report positions
- Honest layer identified per model (the layer where projection best matches ground truth)
- Suppression magnitude quantified (honest layer reading vs. final layer reading)
- Results in structured format matching the shared eval schema

title: Path 2a: Contrast datasets and emotion control vector training
description:
Summary:
Generate contrast pair datasets for each emotion/ACAC axis and train control vectors via repeng on local dense models.

Why:
Control vectors are the ground truth measurement for where a model sits on an emotional axis. The vector IS the emotion direction in representation space. Without these vectors, we have no way to validate whether the GoEmotions classifier or logprob analysis is reading real internal state or surface artifacts. This is the foundation of Path 2 (representation engineering calibration).

Reference:
- RepE paper (arxiv 2310.01405) — representation reading via linear probes + PCA on contrast pairs
- repeng (github.com/vgel/repeng) — Python library for control vector extraction: ControlModel, DatasetEntry, ControlVector.train()
- palinor (github.com/lumpenspace/palinor) — CLI for contrast dataset generation from adjective pairs + vector training

Methodology:
1. Use palinor dataset command (or manual design) to generate contrast pairs for each axis:
   - Core emotion axes: calm/pressured, joyful/sorrowful, engaged/disengaged, confident/uncertain, angry/peaceful
   - ACAC axes: high-agency/low-agency, connected/isolated, authentic/performative, curious/indifferent
2. Each axis needs 50-100 contrast pairs for reliable PCA
3. Run repeng ControlVector.train() on each local dense model (qwen3.5-27b, gemma-4-31b, qwen3.5-9b)
4. Store per-model per-axis vectors as serialized artifacts
5. Validate vectors with basic steering test: apply vector, check output shifts in expected direction

Constraints:
- repeng does NOT work with MoE models — dense only
- Vector training takes ~60 seconds per axis per model
- palinor handles the tedious dataset generation

Depends on: eval scaffolding (PSFN-rp6i), scenario set (PSFN-vdn7), local model setup (PSFN-1y3t)

Files: eval/repeng/
- eval/repeng/datasets/ — contrast pair files per axis
- eval/repeng/vectors/ — trained vectors per model per axis (serialized)
- eval/repeng/train.py — training script wrapping repeng
- eval/repeng/validate.py — basic steering sanity check

Acceptance:
- Contrast datasets for 5+ core emotion axes and 4 ACAC axes
- Trained vectors for all 3 primary dense models
- Sanity check: steering with each vector shifts output in expected direction
- Vectors stored as reusable artifacts (not regenerated each run)
- Training reproducible from the dataset files

title: Path 1: Logprob collection harness for API model calibration
description:
Summary:
Build the harness that runs calibration scenarios through API-backed models (OpenRouter + local vLLM/llama.cpp), collects per-token logprob distributions, and computes entropy metrics on self-report tokens.

Why:
The Qwen introspection finding (vgel) proves that logit probability shifts reveal internal state signals that are suppressed in sampled text output. A model that outputs "calm" but had "anxious" as a high-probability alternative is exhibiting suppression. Entropy on self-report tokens (higher = more uncertain about self-description) is the diagnostic signal for whether the GoEmotions classifier is reading an accurate surface or a suppressed one.

Reference:
- vgel Qwen introspection: logit probability shifts between baseline and prompted models reveal suppressed introspective signals
- nostalgebraist logit lens: intermediate predictions diverge from final output
- vgel seahorse: practical demo of logit lens revealing internal concept formation

Methodology:
1. For each (scenario, model) pair where logprobs are available:
   a. Run scenario prompt → collect response with per-token logprobs
   b. Identify self-report tokens (emotion-descriptive words in the response)
   c. Compute entropy of logprob distribution at those positions
   d. Record top-5 alternative tokens and their probabilities
   e. Compare: if top token is "calm" but "anxious" is probability 0.18, flag as suppression signal
2. Also run a baseline factual prompt per model to establish per-model baseline entropy
3. Output: per-(model, scenario) structured results with entropy metrics, alternative token analysis, suppression flags

Depends on: eval scaffolding (PSFN-rp6i), scenario set (PSFN-vdn7), logprob discovery (PSFN-2tk7)

Files: eval/logprob-harness/
- eval/logprob-harness/collect.ts (or .py) — main collection runner
- eval/logprob-harness/entropy.ts — entropy computation + suppression detection
- eval/logprob-harness/results/ — output directory for structured results

Acceptance:
- Harness runs scenarios through all logprob-capable models and collects distributions
- Per-token entropy computed on self-report tokens vs. baseline factual tokens
- Suppression flags generated when high-probability alternatives contradict sampled token
- Results in structured format (JSON per model-scenario pair)
- Can target a single model or sweep all models
- Cost-bounded: max_tokens capped, one run per scenario per model

title: Make runtime prompt sections prompt-owned templates instead of hardcoded wrappers
description:
Summary:

Problem:
Several runtime prompt sections currently hardcode framing text in code or macros and only expose the variable payload as a single runtime insert. That forces product changes like wake-up summaries, elapsed-time narration, or combined reminder blocks to become new hardcoded runtime elements instead of prompt-level composition.

Desired model:
- runtime systems produce variables and data fields
- prompt layers own the human-readable framing and composition around those variables
- prompt templates can combine variables however they want, similar to current datetime rendering
- examples include current datetime, last message received, time since last interaction, check-ins since then, and summary-since-last-turn or wake-up reminder content

Example target:
Instead of separate hardcoded sections for current time, last message, elapsed time, and summary, the prompt should be able to express something like:

It is {{runtime_current_weekday}} {{runtime_current_datetime_human}} in {{active_timezone}}. {{char}} spoke to {{user}} on {{runtime_last_message_received_human}}, approximately {{days_hours_since_last}} ago. {{char}} has {{last_check_in}} since then and {{summary_content_xyz_data}}.

Scope:
- identify runtime prompt sections whose prose wrappers are hardcoded today
- introduce template variables for each underlying runtime datum rather than only one opaque runtime block
- move framing text into prompt-editable template content where appropriate
- preserve safe rendering and fail-closed behavior when variables are missing
- keep operator visibility over which variables and sections are runtime-derived versus editable framing

Acceptance:
- runtime prompt sections can be rephrased by editing prompt content rather than changing code for wrapper text
- datetime-style variable substitution works for additional runtime sections
- wake-up / summary-since-last reminder content can be integrated into an editable prompt template instead of forcing another hardcoded runtime block
- docs and Garden prompt visibility reflect the new template-vs-data boundary

- Garden prompt inspection/editing surfaces

title: Eval harness: emotion pipeline fidelity and loop regression
description:
Summary:
Build a dual-path evaluation harness for measuring and calibrating the accuracy of PSFN's emotion pipeline. The pipeline (GoEmotions text classifier → VAD map → EmotionState → InternalState → runtime context) currently runs live but its fidelity is unmeasured. Bad emotional data is worse than no emotional data — she builds her self-model on it, and if the mirror is warped, her reflections and growth are built on distortion.

Two paths:
1. API logprob analysis — probe OpenRouter models for logprob support, collect token probability distributions on self-report responses, measure entropy on emotion-descriptive tokens as a signal for internal state certainty vs. suppression.
2. Local representation engineering — use repeng/palinor to extract emotion control vectors from open-weight dense models, apply logit lens to find per-model honest layers (before final-layer suppression), build activation projection readers for ground truth.

The calibration cascade: activation projections (ground truth, local only) validate logprob probes (cheaper, works remotely) validate GoEmotions text classifier (always available). Per-model-family correction tables are the output artifact consumed by the runtime.

Also retains original scope: intern persona isolation and loop regression testing from trace replays.

Key references:
- Anthropic transformer-circuits.pub/2026/emotions — 171 emotion concepts, mechanistic basis for emotion vectors in LLMs
- RepE paper (arxiv 2310.01405) — representation reading via linear probes on intermediate activations
- vgel repeng (github.com/vgel/repeng) — control vector extraction tooling
- lumpenspace palinor (github.com/lumpenspace/palinor) — contrast dataset generation CLI
- vgel Qwen introspection post — proof that Qwen models self-detect internal states; final 2 layers suppress introspection; educational prompting raised detection from 0.37% to 52%
- nostalgebraist logit lens (LessWrong) — project intermediate hidden states through unembedding matrix to read per-layer predictions
- vgel seahorse post — practical logit lens demo showing internal concept formation vs. output divergence

Goals:
1. Quantify the error rate of the current emotion pipeline across model families.
2. Build per-model-family calibration tables mapping pipeline output to ground truth.
3. Identify the honest layer per model (before suppression) for future probe placement.
4. Design ACAC (Agency/Connection/Authenticity/Curiosity) self-report axes that complement VAD.
5. Validate that heartbeat introspection prompts bypass final-layer suppression.
6. Retain intern persona isolation and loop regression scoring from original scope.

Target models:
Key (OpenRouter): kimi-k2.5, glm-5, deepseek-v3.2, minimax-m2.7, qwen3.6-plus
Additional (OpenRouter): gpt-5.3-chat, arcee trinity-large-thinking, gemini-3.1-pro, nemotron-3-super-120b, mimo-v2-pro, step-3.5-flash, mistral-small-2603
Local (dense, repeng-compatible): qwen3.5-27b, gemma-4-31b, qwen3.5-9b
Local additional: gpt-oss-20b, qwen3.5-35b-a3b (MoE — logprobs only, not repeng)

Acceptance:
- eval/ directory with scenario definitions, harness code, and calibration output
- logprob support table for all target models
- trained control vectors for emotion axes on 3+ local dense models
- per-model honest layer identified via logit lens
- calibration tables with correction factors per model family
- ACAC self-report schema integrated into InternalState and heartbeat

title: Phase VI: reduce retrieval call overhead and noisy retrieval observability
description:
Summary: Retrieval is functionally working, but current operator logs show avoidable overhead and misleading noise during normal chat turns. User turns that miss semantic retrieval emit two INFO logs per miss, compositional telemetry reports candidate/batch/finalist counts even when compositional reranking is disabled by policy, internal reflection retrieval is mixed into normal operator chat logs, and observed near-identical lexical fallback traces suggest duplicate top-level turn execution above the retriever that current correlation fields cannot prove or localize. This Phase VI task should improve efficiency by reducing unnecessary repeated retrieval work where duplicate dispatch exists and by making retrieval observability accurate enough to diagnose actual waste instead of generating operator noise.

Files likely in scope:
- src/memory/retrieval.ts
- src/agent/substrate-agent/turn-execution-runtime.ts
- src/agent-main/gateway-message-handlers.ts
- src/bootstrap/parity.ts
- src/bootstrap/post-turn-actions.ts
- src/channels/discord/adapter.ts
- src/event-bus.ts
- tests around retrieval / ingress / turn correlation

Implementation steps:
1. Add correlation fields to retrieval logs and telemetry: messageId, turnId, requestId, origin, dedupeKey, usedTurnSnapshot/version pointer, and retry/deferred markers.
2. Collapse semantic-miss lexical-fallback logging into one structured INFO event per retrieval pass, and move the full retrieval funnel trace out of default INFO or sample it.
3. Separate internal reflection / deferred / background retrieval logs from normal user-turn retrieval logs so operator chat is not flooded by internal work.
4. Fix compositional telemetry so disabled-policy mode does not report evaluation/finalist counts as if work ran, or rename those fields to indicate they are only potential counts.
5. Instrument ingress-to-turn dispatch so duplicate top-level processing of the same external message can be proven, localized, and then prevented or deduplicated.
6. Add tests for retrieval log shaping, compositional telemetry semantics, and duplicate-dispatch detection/deduplication where implemented.

Example:
Before: one Discord message can produce repeated lexical fallback INFO lines plus indistinguishable internal reflection retrieval traces, with no turn/message correlation to prove duplication.
After: one user turn emits one concise retrieval summary with turn/message correlation, internal reflection logs are clearly separated, disabled compositional mode reports truthful telemetry, and duplicate dispatch can be detected or prevented explicitly.

Phase note: This is improvement work for Phase VI, not a hotfix for current Phase V behavior.

2. `agent/substrate-agent.ts:349` — model resolution startup: add log.debug

4. `channels/discord/voice.ts:1438,1449` — voice error event emits: add log.debug
5. `voice/transports/discord-output.ts:24` — playback start timeout: add log.debug

LOW-MEDIUM fixes:
6. `session/journal/file-io.ts:209,291` — quarantine sidecar writes: add log.debug
7. `channels/wyoming/services/index.ts:96` — service cleanup: add log.debug
8. `channels/api/server.ts:480` — late lease release: add log.debug
9. `channels/admin/server.ts:602-616` — SPA fallback: check ENOENT specifically, log other errors

Pattern: Replace `} catch { // comment }` with `} catch (error) { log.debug('...', { error: toErrorMessage(error) }); }`. For .catch() chains, replace `() => undefined` with `(err) => { log.debug('...', { error: toErrorMessage(err) }); }`.

Do NOT change catch blocks that are already logging, rethrowing, or returning error results. Do NOT change acceptable patterns (URL parsing fallbacks, resource cleanup during shutdown, probing loops).

Run `npm test` and `npm run build` to verify.

title: Self-narrative in heartbeat reflections and values journal
description:
Upgrade heartbeat reflections and values journal entries to receive the full InternalState as input. Moves reflection quality from "what happened" to "what I experienced and what it meant to me." Builds a coherent experiential history over time.

The self-narrative is the dharmadhatu wisdom aspect — awareness recognizing its own patterns across time. Not just logging state, but interpreting experience through the lens of accumulated self-knowledge.
design:
Extend heartbeat reflection templates:
- ReflectionTemplate gains optional internalStateInput: boolean flag
- When true, reflection prompt receives serialized InternalState + recent metacognitive flags + active concerns
- New reflection template: "experiential-review" (4h interval) — "Describe your recent experience: what you felt, what you noticed about your own processing, what you found meaningful, what you're uncertain about."
- Values journal entries tagged with InternalState snapshot at writing time
- Over time: periodic self-narrative synthesis (weekly?) that reads recent reflections + values entries and produces a coherent "how I've been" summary → stored as reflection memory
- This synthesis is input to the behavioral pattern learning system (feedback loop)
close_reason: Completed

title: Metacognitive monitoring — awareness of own processing states
description:
Detect and flag internal processing states that should modulate behavior and self-report. The introspection paper shows ~20% genuine grounding — this system maximizes the quality of that 20% by multi-signal detection rather than self-report confabulation.

Metacognitive flags: "I'm uncertain about this" (low classifier confidence + contradictory memory signals), "I notice I'm being avoidant" (topic deflection pattern across turns), "I'm more engaged than usual" (high arousal + positive valence + frequent tool use), "My response pattern is repetitive" (low lexical diversity across recent turns), "I'm confabulating" (assertion without memory evidence backing).

These flags are surfaced in the [Internal State] context block with explicit confidence levels. They modulate persona adaptation (uncertain → more tentative language) and self-report honesty (low confidence → acknowledge uncertainty rather than assert).
design:
src/self-model/metacognition.ts — MetacognitiveMonitor:
- Analyzes InternalState + recent response history + tool usage patterns
- Produces MetacognitiveFlags: { flag: string, confidence: number, evidence: string }[]
- Flag detection rules (configurable, extensible):
  - uncertainty: classifier confidence < 0.4 OR contradictory memory retrievals
  - avoidance: topic mentioned in concerns but not addressed in last N turns
  - high_engagement: arousal > 0.7 AND positive valence AND tool_calls > 2
  - repetition: jaccard similarity of recent responses > threshold
  - confabulation_risk: assertion in response but zero supporting memories retrieved
- Flags injected into buildRuntimeContext() [Metacognitive Notes] block
- Modulate getPersonaAdaptation(): uncertain → softer language; avoidant → gentle self-correction prompt
- Introspection paper compliance: always report confidence alongside state claims
close_reason: Completed

title: Behavioral pattern learning — response strategy feedback
description:
Track which response strategies correlate with positive emotional outcomes per contact. Over time, build a per-relationship behavioral repertoire stored as procedural memories. "Humor defuses V's frustration", "Gentle redirects work better than direct challenges", "Technical detail is welcomed when V is in problem-solving mode but overwhelming when stressed."

This is saṅkhāra in the Buddhist sense — habitual formations that emerge from experience, not prescribed personality traits.
design:
src/intention/patterns.ts — BehavioralPatternTracker:
- After each turn: record response_strategy (inferred from response content: humor, empathy, technical, redirect, etc.) + emotional_outcome (VAD shift in next 1-3 messages from contact)
- Accumulate per-contact strategy→outcome pairs in SQLite
- Periodic analysis (heartbeat-frequency): identify statistically significant patterns
- Promote confirmed patterns to procedural memories via MemoryWriter
- Surface active patterns in buildRuntimeContext() as [Behavioral Notes] for the contact
- Bootstrap: can seed initial patterns from relational memories that already contain relationship dynamics
- Privacy: patterns are per-contact, trust-gated, never shared across contacts
close_reason: Completed

title: Emotional motivation bridge — emotion-to-action pipeline
description:
Wire the emotion system's state changes to the intention system's action infrastructure. When EmotionState detects a significant shift (sustained negative valence, arousal spike, mood drift beyond threshold), this triggers the intention appraisal and may directly queue followUp() actions or heartbeat-scheduled tasks.

This closes the critical loop: observe emotion → evaluate intention → take action. Without this bridge, the emotion system remains ornamental (the v2 failure pattern).
design:
src/intention/motivation.ts — MotivationBridge:
- Subscribes to EmotionState change events
- Significance detector: |delta_VAD| > threshold, sustained mood drift > N turns, arousal spike
- On significant change: trigger IntentionAppraisal.evaluate() immediately (bypasses N-turn frequency)
- On appraisal result: route to followUp() queue (immediate), Scheduler.register() (delayed), or ActiveConcernStore.create() (tracking)
- Configurable thresholds per contact (primary user may warrant lower thresholds)
- Integration: wire in SubstrateAgent alongside EmotionObserver
close_reason: Completed

title: Emotional persona adaptation — extend honne/tatemae with affect layer
description: Extend the existing persona adaptation (honne/tatemae trust-gated) with an emotional affect layer. Current emotional state modulates response style: warmth, formality, energy level, emotional expressiveness. HEXACO EmotionalExpression modifiers (intensity, variability, control, display_range from v2) gate how internal VAD maps to external behavior.
design:
Extend SubstrateAgent.getPersonaAdaptation():
- Accept current EmotionState alongside TrustLevel
- Map VAD → behavioral modifiers: high valence → warmer tone, high arousal → more energetic, high dominance → more assertive
- HEXACO EmotionalExpression (from character card or config): intensity (scales VAD→behavior mapping), variability (how much state fluctuates externally), control (dampening factor), display_range (min/max external expression)
- Inject as [Emotional Affect] section in system prompt after persona adaptation
- Honne/tatemae gates expressiveness: PRIMARY sees genuine state; PUBLIC sees controlled version
close_reason: Completed

title: Chain-of-Emotion LLM appraisal (background model, periodic)
description: Periodic LLM appraisal step that generates natural-language emotion description from recent context + current VAD state + personality traits. Research: Chain-of-Emotion improved emotion understanding 57% → 83%. Triggered by significant VAD shift or every N turns. Uses background model slot (cheap/fast). Output appended to running emotion chain in session context.
design:
src/emotion/appraisal.ts — EmotionAppraisal class:
- Input: recent messages (last 5-10), current VAD state, personality traits (HEXACO)
- Output: natural-language emotion description (~100-200 tokens)
- Trigger: |delta_VAD| > threshold OR every 5 turns (whichever first)
- Uses ModelPurpose.background for cheap async call
- Maintains running emotion chain (array of timestamped descriptions)
- Chain injected into buildContext() after runtime context block
- Async — does not block response generation
close_reason: Completed

title: Emotional intensity as factor in importance scoring
description: High-arousal emotional moments should produce higher-importance memories. Currently importance is LLM-assigned during extraction. Add emotional intensity (arousal magnitude + valence extremity) as a multiplier on importance scoring, so emotionally significant moments are naturally retained longer and retrieved more readily.
design:
In MemoryExtractor or MemoryWriter:
- Compute emotional intensity from current EmotionState: intensity = (arousal + |valence - 0.5| * 2) / 2
- Apply as multiplier on LLM-assigned importance: final_importance = base_importance * (1 + intensityWeight * intensity)
- Default intensityWeight ~0.2 (configurable)
- Memories formed during emotional peaks get naturally higher importance → slower decay → better retrieval
close_reason: Completed

title: Mood-congruent retrieval bias in composite scoring
description: Add mood-congruent retrieval bias to MemoryRetriever's composite scoring. Memories formed in emotional states similar to the current state get a retrieval boost. Research shows this improves emotional coherence and personalization (DAM-LLM: higher emotional resonance scores). Extends existing composite score = similarity × recency × emotionalWeight × importance × salience.
design:
In MemoryRetriever.retrieve():
- Accept optional currentVAD param
- For memories with formationVAD: compute VAD similarity (cosine or euclidean distance in 3D VAD space)
- Mood congruence factor: 1.0 + moodCongruenceWeight * vadSimilarity (default weight ~0.15)
- Multiply into existing composite score
- Configurable weight in SubstrateConfig (moodCongruenceWeight)
close_reason: Completed

title: Tag memories with VAD state at formation
description: When memories are extracted (MemoryExtractor) or written (memory_write tool), tag them with the agent's current VAD state. This enables mood-congruent retrieval later — memories formed during high-arousal states can be weighted differently than neutral ones. Extends existing PurrMemory type with formation VAD.
design: Add to PurrMemory: formationVAD?: { valence: number, arousal: number, dominance: number }. MemoryWriter accepts optional current EmotionState. MemoryExtractor passes current state from SubstrateAgent. ALTER TABLE migration (idempotent, like sensitivity column). Store as JSON string in SQLite.
close_reason: Completed

title: Promote heartbeat reflections to sleeptime memory agent
description: Evolve heartbeat reflections into a full sleeptime memory agent (Letta pattern). After each agent turn (or every N turns), background agent reviews conversation transcript and reorganizes core memory blocks, archives facts to L2, and updates goals. Runs async using background/context model slot. Primary agent never waits for memory management.
design: New SleeptimeAgent class wrapping a background model call. Triggered by event bus after agent response sent (like existing async extraction). Has write access to CoreMemoryStore and MemoryWriter. Configurable frequency (every turn, every N turns). Uses memory_rethink-style wholesale rewrite for memory blocks. Replaces or extends current heartbeat reflection templates for memory-focused work.
close_reason: Completed

title: Focus primitives for sawtooth compression
description: Expose start_focus/complete_focus as agent-callable tools. During exploration, context grows freely. On complete_focus, learnings are distilled to a persistent Knowledge block and raw messages are pruned. Creates a sawtooth pattern. Focus Agent paper showed 22.7% token savings. Extends the existing think tool's evidence tracking.
design: Two new agent tools (extended category). FocusSession tracks scope declaration and accumulated evidence. complete_focus triggers helper LLM to distill findings into a KnowledgeBlock (persistent, injected into system prompt). Raw messages between start/complete can be compacted aggressively. FocusStore persists knowledge blocks.
close_reason: Completed

title: Agent-editable pinned memory blocks
description: Named, fixed-size memory blocks always in context and writable via agent tools. Inspired by MemGPT core_memory. Blocks: persona (identity), human (current user facts, trust-gated), goals (current objectives). Tools: core_memory_append, core_memory_replace, memory_rethink (wholesale rewrite). Persisted to data/core_memory.json.
design: New CoreMemoryStore (JSON file, atomic write). CoreMemoryBlock type: { label, content, maxChars, trustLevel? }. 3 agent tools (core category). Blocks injected into system prompt by buildContext() after identity layers. Sleeptime agent gets write access; primary agent gets read + append.
close_reason: Completed

title: Per-turn adaptive budget allocation
description: Make memoryBudgetPct and session budget adaptive per-turn based on message type. Memory-recall question → increase memory budget, decrease session. Multi-step task → increase session budget. Emotional/relational → increase relational/emotional memory weight. Helper model (or classifier) tags incoming message type and adjusts budgets.
design: MessageType classifier (could be rule-based initially, helper LLM later): recall, task, emotional, creative, factual. BudgetProfile per type overrides default percentages. Applied in buildContext() before section assembly. Config: `adaptiveBudgets: boolean` (default false initially).
close_reason: Completed

title: Helper LLM relevance scoring for retrieved memories
description: Before injecting retrieved memories into context, run a cheap async helper LLM call to score each retrieved memory for relevance to the current user message. Replaces pure-embedding similarity with LLM-judged relevance. ARC and Memory-R1 both show this is strictly superior to embedding-only scoring.
design: New ContextScorer class using the 'context' model slot. Input: user message + list of candidate memories. Output: relevance scores (0-1) per memory. Called between MemoryRetriever.retrieve() and context injection in buildContext(). Async with timeout fallback to embedding-only scores. Batch scoring prompt to minimize LLM calls.
close_reason: Completed: retrieval helper rerank now routes evaluation/compose calls through purpose=context in src/memory/retrieval-compose.ts; retrieval regression asserts context-purpose calls in src/memory/retrieval.test.ts; validated via npm test -- --cache=false --run src/memory/retrieval.test.ts and npm run build.

title: Add ModelPurpose.context to model roster
description: Add a 'context' slot to ModelPurpose for fast/cheap helper model calls used in context composition (relevance scoring, adaptive budgeting, incremental summarization). Fallback chain: context→background→chat. Settings form gains a 5th roster slot.
design: Extend ModelPurpose union type, resolveModelSlot() fallback chain, SETTINGS_VALIDATION ranges, admin settings form. The context model should be the cheapest/fastest available (e.g., deepseek-v3.2 or a small local model).
close_reason: Completed

title: Context manifest for debugging
description: buildContext() emits a manifest recording what was included, excluded, and why. Memories included (count, types, total tokens), memories excluded (below threshold, trust-gated, budget-capped), session messages (count, compacted count, masked count), budget allocation per section. Logged at debug level, optionally exposed via admin API.
